question: CallSage worker not writing logs to configured log directory on Linux
answer: The issue is that systemd does not automatically read .env files. Even though your .env has the correct log paths, the service never knew about them, so the worker defaulted to its internal log path.  Fix: Add the .env file to the service with EnvironmentFile:  [Service] User=ec2-user WorkingDirectory=/opt/tetherfi/callsage EnvironmentFile=/opt/tetherfi/callsage/.env Environment="PATH=/opt/tetherfi/callsage/venv/bin:/usr/bin" ExecStart=/opt/tetherfi/callsage/venv/bin/python /opt/tetherfi/callsage/callsage_launcher.py Restart=always Then reload and restart:  sudo systemctl daemon-reload sudo systemctl restart callsage After this, logs will be written correctly to /opt/tetherfi/logs/callsage.

question: Windows service set to Automatic (Delayed Start) still fails to start after reboot with “service did not respond in a timely fashion”
answer: This is a Windows Service Control Manager (SCM) timeout issue, not a problem with the service itself.  By default, Windows waits 30 seconds (30000 ms) for a service to report that it has started. If the service performs heavy startup work (such as certificate loading, cryptography, or database initialization), it may exceed this limit during system boot, causing Windows to mark it as failed—even though it would have started successfully if given more time. question: Do we have any high level Login logic flow Tmac UI,Proxy and Tmac server
answer: AGENT UI | | Login Request (AgentID, StationID, Credentials) v TMAC SDK PROXY  Collects session count from all TMAC servers Selects TMAC server with lowest active sessions | v TMAC SERVER | |-- Create Agent Session |-- Load Agent Template & Operating Hours | |-- CTI / TSAPI Initialization | * SecurityLogout | * SecurityLogin | * MonitorStation | * AgentLogin | |-- Agent Login Success | |-- CheckStationValidity | * Config enabled? | * Validation number present? | * CTI type check (non SIP/DUMMY) | * Station type filter | * Make outbound call | * Disconnect the call | |-- Register with Managers (To register agent session with all the managers, so it can received events example wallboard events,notification events ,Agent status change event ,etc..) | * Recorder Manager | * Interaction Manager | * Agent Status Manager | |-- Agent Session Active | v Login Success Response | v AGENT UI (Logged In) The agent login flow starts when the Agent UI sends a login request to the TMAC SDK Proxy, which acts as a routing layer. The SDK Proxy checks the active session count across all available TMAC servers and forwards the request to the TMAC server with the lowest load. The selected TMAC Server then owns the complete login lifecycle: it creates the agent session, loads the agent template and operating-hours configuration, initializes the CTI/TSAPI stack, performs PBX security login, monitors the station, and executes the agent login. Once the agent login is successful, the server performs an optional CheckStationValidity step based on configuration, station type, and CTI login type; this validation is done by initiating a test outbound call from the station and disconnecting it on success, ensuring the station is usable before proceeding. If the station is valid, the agent is registered with internal managers such as the recorder, interaction, and agent status managers, the session is marked active, and a successful login response is returned back through the SDK Proxy to the Agent UI, completing the end-to-end login flow.

question: How does the OCM Pending Email Ageing Report calculate pending emails and ageing buckets?
answer: The OCM Pending Email Ageing Report shows only pending (unattended) emails—emails that are received but not answered or closed at the time the report is generated. Closed or replied emails are not included.  Key behavior: Single Date selection Shows only emails received on that specific date that are still pending today. Ageing is calculated using the report run date, not the selected date.  Date Range selection Shows a cumulative backlog of emails received on any day within the selected range that are still pending today. This is not a daily snapshot, which is why older emails can appear.  Ageing calculation: Ageing buckets are calculated as: Report Run Date – Email Received Date  Example:  Email received on 15-Dec, report run on 17-Dec → 2 days old  Email received on 12-Dec, report run on 17-Dec → 5 days old  Additional points: An email may appear in a range report but not a single-date report because the single-date report only considers emails received on that one day.  The Oldest Email column shows the earliest received pending email for a skill, helping identify how long the oldest backlog item has been waiting.  In summary: The report represents the current backlog of pending emails received during the selected date or date range, with ageing always calculated as of the report generation date.

question: 'telnet' is not recognized on Windows — how do I enable Telnet and test port 450 step-by-step?
answer: 'telnet' is not recognized means the Telnet client is not installed/enabled on your Windows. Follow these steps to enable it and test the port — plus alternatives if you can't or don't want to use Telnet.  1) Open an elevated shell (Admin) Why: enabling features requires admin privileges.  Steps  Click Start → type cmd  Right-click Command Prompt → Run as administrator  Confirm any UAC prompt. Confirm the title bar shows:  Administrator: Command Prompt  2) Enable Telnet using DISM (recommended) Command (type only — do not include C:\...> prompt):  dism /online /Enable-Feature /FeatureName:TelnetClient Expected output (success):  Enabling feature(s) [==========================100.0%==========================] The operation completed successfully. Common errors  Error 740 or Access is denied. → you are not running an elevated prompt. Reopen Command Prompt as Administrator and retry.  If DISM fails for other reasons, try the PowerShell method below.  3) Alternative: Enable via PowerShell (Admin) Open PowerShell as Administrator and run:  Enable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName TelnetClient You’ll be prompted to restart in some builds (rare). Accept if asked.  4) Alternative: Enable via GUI Open Control Panel → Programs and Features  Click Turn Windows features on or off  Check Telnet Client → OK → wait for install to finish  5) Verify Telnet is available and test connection After enabling, in a regular Command Prompt run:  telnet 10.133.146.60 450 Results  If connection succeeds: screen goes blank (cursor blinking). That means the TCP handshake succeeded.  To exit telnet, press Ctrl+] then type quit and Enter. If it fails: you’ll see Could not open connection to the host, on port 450: Connect failed — indicates the port is closed/filtered or host unreachable.  Repeat for the second host:  telnet 10.133.146.62 450 6) Recommended (and easier) alternative: PowerShell Test-NetConnection If you prefer a simple, scriptable test that doesn’t require Telnet, use PowerShell:  Test-NetConnection -ComputerName 10.133.146.60 -Port 450 Test-NetConnection -ComputerName 10.133.146.62 -Port 450 Look for:  TcpTestSucceeded : True If False, the port is unreachable (firewall, network route, or service down).  7) Troubleshooting checklist if port unreachable Can you ping the host? ping 10.133.146.60 (ICMP may be blocked — not definitive).  Is the service listening on the host? (Check server-side: netstat -an | findstr 450)  Is a host firewall blocking port 450? (Windows Firewall / iptables / network ACL)  Is there a network ACL or route blocking between your machine and the host?  If testing from a corporate laptop, check local outbound firewall or proxy restrictions.  Try Test-NetConnection -TraceRoute -ComputerName <ip> to verify routing.  8) Example scenario (full flow) Open Admin cmd.  Run: dism /online /Enable-Feature /FeatureName:TelnetClient → success.  Open regular cmd and run: telnet 10.133.146.60 450 → blank screen = OK.  If telnet fails, in PowerShell run: Test-NetConnection -ComputerName 10.133.146.60 -Port 450 → check TcpTestSucceeded.  9) Short summary (quick copy) Enable Telnet (Admin): dism /online /Enable-Feature /FeatureName:TelnetClient  Or PowerShell (no telnet): Test-NetConnection -ComputerName 10.133.146.60 -Port 450

question: Purodex Archive Job Failing With NullReferenceException in ProcessBatchAsync Due to Linked Server Issue
answer: This error was caused by a missing or incorrectly configured SQL Server Linked Server, which Purodex requires to move data between:  Online DB  Archival DB  Why the error occurred During archival, Purodex uses stored procedures that rely on a linked server to insert historical data into the Archival database.  The call that fails:  DatabaseService.ExecuteProcAsync(DatabaseType.Archive, ...) fails because the stored procedure internally references a linked server name that does not exist on the SQL Server instance.  As a result:  The stored procedure cannot execute  SQL returns no result object  Purodex receives a NULL result  Purodex throws:  System.NullReferenceException: Object reference not set to an instance of an object. Fix Create the correct Linked Server on SQL Server, matching the name Purodex expects (from TMC_Data.json). There is a stack already on how to create Linked Server.  Outcome Once the linked server existed and matched the configured name:  ExecuteProcAsync executed correctly  Stored procedures ran without errors  All batches were processed  Archival for TMAC_WorkQueueHistory completed successfully

question: Purodex Archive Job Failing With System.NullReferenceException During Reporting DB Connectivity Check
answer: The error was caused by an incorrect or missing Reporting Database connection string in the Purodex configuration file (TMC_Data.json).  Even though the linked server was configured correctly, Purodex performs a three-way database connectivity check at startup:  Online DB  Reporting DB  Archival DB  If any one of these fails, the entire archive attempt is aborted and Purodex shows:  One or all database connectivity failed, aborting. In my case, the error originated from this method:  Purodex.Database.DatabaseConnectivityService.CheckDatabaseConnectivity() A NullReferenceException here means that Purodex could not create a valid SQL connection object for the Reporting DB because the connection string it read was null.  Root Cause In TMC_Data.json, the entry:  "ReportingDbConnectionString": "" was either empty, misnamed, or pointing to the wrong Reporting DB.  This caused the internal Reporting DB object to be null → which throws:  System.NullReferenceException: Object reference not set to an instance of an object. Fix I updated TMC_Data.json with the correct Reporting DB connection string:  "ReportingDbConnectionString": "Server=<server>;Database=<ReportingDB>;User Id=...;Password=...;TrustServerCertificate=True;" After restarting Purodex:  Reporting DB connectivity passed  IVR_Usage and other Reporting tables were processed  Archive batches executed successfully  NullReferenceException disappeared  Outcome Archival completed normally once the ReportingDbConnectionString was corrected.

question: Cannot connect to MySQL database - Unsupported protocol version when connecting to MySQL in .NET
answer: The error “Unsupported protocol version” appears when the MySQL client library (MySql.Data or MySqlConnector) tries to connect using the classic MySQL protocol, but the port specified in the connection string does not support that protocol.  Later, after checking the MySQL configuration, I found that the server was actually listening on port 5886. When I updated the connection string to use that port, the error disappeared and the connection succeeded.  Root Cause:  Port 3306 is the default MySQL port for the classic protocol.  Port 33060 is for the MySQL X Protocol (used by MySQL Shell and X DevAPI). The .NET MySQL connectors do not support X Protocol.  If MySQL is configured to use a custom port (like 5886), that same port must be used in the connection string.  Connecting to the wrong port causes a failed handshake and results in “Unsupported protocol version.”  Steps to Troubleshoot:  Check the actual MySQL port Log in to the MySQL server and run: SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'port'; This command displays the port MySQL is listening on. Example output: port = 5886  Update your connection string Update the port number to match the value from the previous step. Example: Provider=mysql;Server=host.docker.internal;Port=5886;Database=ocm;User Id=root;Password=@Shetty6885;SslMode=None;AllowPublicKeyRetrieval=True;  Verify connectivity From your host machine, test the same connection using the MySQL command line: mysql -h host.docker.internal -P 5886 -u root -p If this connects successfully, the .NET application should also work.  Restart your .NET service After updating the connection string, restart the service. The connection should now open successfully.

question: All CM Connectivity Failed, Please Check the configuration and set valid CM User Credentials in SMS API
answer: This error occurs during the connection between the SMS API service and Avaya AES/Communication Manager (CM) when the API fails to establish a valid session.  In the SMS API, there is a service URL configured to connect with AES, which in turn communicates with CM. The connection uses the service URL, CM IP address, username, and password to send a SOAP request (Submit Request) and fetch the Hunt Group details.  During this process, the API reads the CM_SkillRange from the configuration and uses the first skill ID from that range while performing the SOAP request.  For example:  If CM_SkillRange = 6000-6100, the first skill ID used will be 6000.  If CM_SkillRange = 6000-6100,7000-7300, the first skill ID used will still be 6000 (the first in the first range).  You’ll see the error “All CM Connectivity Failed, Please Check the configuration and set valid CM User Credentials” when:  The Service URL is incorrect,  The CM username or password is invalid, or  The first skill ID from the configured range does not exist in CM.

question: Why is my OCMUI - ASP.NET Core web app not writing logs to a file even though Serilog is configured?
answer: This usually happens because the IIS application pool identity does not have permission to create the log file itself, even if the folder already exists. When Serilog starts, it tries to create or open the file. If that fails, it silently drops the file sink without throwing an exception unless you enable SelfLog.  Here’s a verified checklist that resolves the issue:  Grant explicit file permissions to the App Pool identity  icacls "D:\APPBASE\UCISG\App_log" /grant "IIS AppPool\SG_UCI_OCMUI:(OI)(CI)F" /T icacls "D:\APPBASE\UCISG\App_log" /grant "IIS_IUSRS:(OI)(CI)F" /T  Then recycle the app pool.  Ensure the directory actually exists Serilog won’t create nested directories by default. Create the full path:  D:\APPBASE\UCISG\App_log\SG_UCI_OCMUI  Check disk space Serilog silently fails if the volume is full. Ensure at least a few hundred MB free.  Verify that logger.json is actually loaded  Once permissions and the path are correct, the file will appear on the next log event.

question: TMAC UI shows “Destination is null” error when user is gets locked for any reason
answer: The “Destination is null” error in TMAC UI typically occured due to underlying authentication or CTI connectivity issues or any, even though the UI showed destination null error, but logs said that user as locked.  From our scenario experience and logs analysis, the common causes are:  Invalid or misconfigured LDAP:  TMAC uses LDAP to authenticate users.  If the LDAP server published in Service Discovery is incorrect or unreachable, TMAC cannot verify credentials.  Logs show errors like:  Unable to connect to server <IP>:389 LdapException: An existing connection was forcibly closed by the remote host  User login attempts exceeding the threshold:  After multiple failed login attempts, TMAC may temporarily treat the user as locked.  Logs may display:  User is locked  Troubleshooting steps: Check TMAC server logs:  Look for LDAP connection error or SecurityLogin failed. Verify LDAP configuration:  Ensure the correct LDAP server is published in Service Discovery.  Confirm that the user DN, base DN, and credentials are correct.  Test LDAP bind using PowerShell or any LDAP client.  Clear invalid or duplicate login attempts:  Remove unwanted test login entries in the TMAC database. Validate CTI/TSAPI server:  Confirm the correct PBX/TSAPI server address and port.  Ensure the agent is mapped to a valid station/extension and has TSAPI permissions.  Retry login after changes:  Once LDAP and CTI/TSAPI settings are corrected, the login should succeed.  TMAC UI should no longer display Destination is null.  Summary:  “Destination is null” often indicates a CTI/Voice server or LDAP connectivity issue  Correcting LDAP configuration or any reason for tmac failure and CTI server mapping resolves the issue.

question: How does AES recovery work in CTI Server and TMAC Server?
answer: Tetherfi CTI Server connects to Avaya AES using TSAPI client libraries and creates a TCP connection over port 1050.  The session between CTI server and AES can break:  If CTI server to AES network disconnects  If AES to CM connection breaks  In either case, CTI Server gets to know that the session is broken.  When this happens, CTI Server sends a "OnSessionFailed" event to all the TMAC web socket connections (agent sessions).  Upon receiving the event, the TSAPI Client Library in TMAC server starts a loop to keep calling the "SecurityLogin" method in regular intervals. This is done based on below TMAC config:  <add key="DoAESRecovery" value="true" /> <add key="AESRecoveryLoopTime" value="20" /> <add key="AESRecoveryMaxLoops" value="15" /> When TSAPI Client Lib is able to get a successful response for "SecurityLogin", then it will inform the corresponding agent sessions with a "OnSessionUp" event. And each agent session will perform a "monitor station" command to start receiving events again.

question: Why doesn't the Web.config file get updated automatically when we recycle or stop and start the application pool using IIS or TMC?
answer: Technically, the Web.config file is not updated or reloaded immediately when the application pool is recycled or restarted in IIS or through TMC. Instead, the configuration settings in Web.config are only read and applied when the application receives its first request after the restart. when using tmc config loader  TConfig Loader Behavior – Technical Overview  Upon application startup, the TConfig Loader is triggered automatically when application start or program main. Its primary role is to process configuration templates using solution-specific values defined in tmc.data.json. The flow is as follows:  The loader reads the template configuration file (e.g., web.template.config) and substitutes keys with values from tmc.data.json.  The processed data is then used to overwrite the actual config file specified in tmc.config (typically web.config, appsettings.json, etc.).  This operation happens once, specifically when the first request reaches IIS (i.e., during the application pool's cold start).  In contrast, for Windows Services, the TConfig Loader does not rely on an incoming request to initiate. The configuration replacement happens immediately during service initialization/startup.

question: How does TMAC server load balancing and high availability work?
answer: Load Balancing  We can have more than one TMAC server running at the same time.  When the Agent Desktop or the TMAC UI tries to login to a TMAC server, the TMAC proxy has the ability to distribute the logins across TMAC servers.  In non-SD mode, the TMAC Proxy does this Login distribution based on below configurations:  <add key="TmacServerTrySequence" value="1,2" />  <add key="ServerCapacityRatio" value="1:1" />  The “TmacServerTrySequence” contains the list of TMAC servers and the order. The “ServerCapacityRatio” provides the login count ratio between these two TMAC servers. In the above example, we have 2 TMAC servers and the ratio to share the load is 50-50.  First the TMAC proxy first calls both TMAC servers to get the current session counts, and then based on above configs, it will decide which TMAC server should get the next login request.  In SD mode, TMAC proxy does not use the “ServerCapacityRatio”. It first calls all TMAC servers to get the current session counts, and then sends the Login command to the TMAC with the least number of sessions.  So in SD mode, the load is equally distributed among all TMAC servers.  High Availability  When there are multiple TMAC servers running, agent logins are distributed among these TMAC servers. In case one of these TMAC servers fails due to expected reason, the solution has the ability to move the sessions of the failed TMAC server to the other TMAC servers.  To do this, TMAC server uses a concept called “Interaction Recovery Data”. When a new Interaction is created in TMAC server, it also creates a data object called “Interaction Recovery Data” that includes the minimum data required to recover an Interaction. And this data object is sent to the UI (TMAC UI or Agent Desktop) as part of Incoming Interaction events and the TMAC JS SDK saves these data in the UI memory.  Detecting a failure  Detecting a TMAC server failure happens in two different ways based on the event protocol used between the UI and the server.  When using getEvent polling (long polling or short polling), the UI for an agent login calls the “getEvent” method in TMAC proxy and the TMAC proxy calls the “getEvent” method of TMAC server. When TMAC proxy detects a TMAC server “getEvent” method call failure due to a 404 or request timeout, it tries to call the same “getEvent” method 10 more times to ensure the failure is due to TMAC server unavailability  (and not some network failure that happened for a split of a second). If all 10 requests fail then TMAC proxy treats it as a complete TMAC server failure and decides to move the agent to another healthy TMAC server.  When using a SignalR socket for events, the TMAC SDK detects a SignalR socket failure. And it has inbuilt mechanisms to try connecting again. After trying to reconnect and if it is not able to reconnect, the TMAC SDK calls the “GetTMACServerOnSocketFail” method in the TMAC proxy. The TMAC Proxy then checks if the TMAC server is available by calling TMAC server’s “GetAgentSession” method. If the TMAC server responds then TMAC proxy responds back to UI (TMAC SDK) with a “TmacServerConnectionExist” event and the SDK tries to connect to SignalR again.  If the TMAC server “GetAgentSession” fails, then TMAC proxy treats that the TMAC server has failed. Then the TMAC Proxy will try to login the agent to the next available TMAC server. The next available TMAC server is fetched from “TmacServerTrySequence” in non-SD mode and from service registry in SD mode.  In both above scenarios (eventPolling or SignalR), after successfully login into a new TMAC server, the Proxy sends an “TmacServerConnectionSuccess” event to TMAC SDK with new TMAC server details. The SDK will update its local references of the tmac server and restart getEvent polling or reconnect to the new SignalR endpoint.  Interaction Recovery  After getting a “TmacServerConnectionSuccess”, the TMAC SDK connects to the new TMAC server over SignalR or via TMAC proxy. And then it calls the “RecoverInteractions” method of the TMAC server via the TMAC proxy. The UI sends the previously saved “Interaction Recovery Data” for all open interactions in the UI in this method. Once the new TMAC server received these data in “RecoverInteractions” method, it will create the interactions in the agent session. And then the UI can continue the interaction from when it was stopped.  Ref:  https://docs.google.com/document/d/1p1zoi85gmIYi180qmQ8gzCVZRVo72uR2JDvxJxmP_Uo/edit?usp=sharing

question: Campaign Manager: SIP re-INVITE Fails
answer: Issue:  The campaign adds a contact to the queue, and the SIP INVITE contains the private IP of the Campaign Manager application server. Contacts remain in the queue because no agents are available. The Communication Manager (CM) initiates a re-INVITE to the campaign based on the session timeout configured in Avaya CM. The Session Manager (SM) attempts to send the re-INVITE to the private IP received in the initial invite from the campaign. However, because only NAT IPs are configured in the SM, it cannot route the re-INVITE to the Campaign Manager. Due to the lack of response to the re-INVITE, the call session times out. However, once agents become available, these queued calls are still routed to the agent. The campaign tries to send a BYE signal once the call is routed to an agent, but the BYE signal fails. Since the BYE signal does not reach the CM, the calls are not disconnected. Solution:  Campaign Manager Limitation:  The Campaign Manager is only a SIP client; it is not a listener. Therefore, re-INVITE requests cannot be handled or processed. Steps to Address the Issue:  Queue Contact Condition:  Ensure that contacts are added to the queue based on the availability of TMAC staffed agents. This configuration can be set in the Campaign Settings. Queue Timeout at Campaign Level:  Set the queue timeout to the Average Call Handle Time + Buffer. Example: Average Call Handle Time = 10 minutes Queue Timeout = 11 minutes (1 minute is considered as buffer) Vector Queue Time Configuration:  Add queue time in the vector to handle scenarios where the queued item is not removed from the Campaign Manager. The queue time should be Campaign Queue Time + Buffer. Example: Campaign Level Queue Timeout = 11 minutes Vector Level Queue Timeout = 12 minutes (1 minute is considered as buffer) Separate Trunk for Campaign:  Create a separate trunk specifically for the campaign. Session Timeout for Campaign Trunk:  Extend the session timeout of the campaign trunk to the vector-level queue timeout + buffer. Example: Vector Level Queue Timeout = 12 minutes Trunk Level Session Timeout = 13 minutes (1 minute is considered as buffer) Conclusion: By following this approach, the need to handle re-INVITE requests from the Communication Manager (CM) can be avoided.

question: TPPVA: difference between UseDirectSynonymSearch=1 and UseDirectSynonymSearch=0 config key value
answer: The key "UseDirectSynonymSearch" is used to manage the type of decision making that involves synonyms when trying to find the intent of the user's freetext message. This is only applicable when user has typed a freetext, which means chatbot mode has to be enabled in VIVR and the user has to enter a freetext.  Difference between UseDirectSynonymSearch=1 and UseDirectSynonymSearch=0  UseDirectSynonymSearch=0, Menu search Intent based on the synonym having match <60% with the freetext could be found in the current (local) menu. Therefore, whichever synonym has the greatest match percentage with the freetext will be selected. This could have two possibilities:  if only one intent is found with the highest matching percentage in the current menu, then user will be directly navigated to that option which satisfies the above condition as well (synonyms matching <60% is mandatory). For example, - option 1 has matching percentage of 70% - option 2 has matching percentage of 85% then option 2 will be selected  if two or more intents are found with the highest match percentage in the current menu, then user will be prompted with the option of intents which satisfies the above condition as well (synonyms matching <60% is mandatory). For example, - option 1 has matching percentage of 70% - option 2 has matching percentage of 70% - option 3 has matching percentage of 60% then user will be prompted with "Did you mean option1 or option2"  Global search If intent is not found in the current menu satisfying the above condition, then intent based on the synonym having a match <60% with the freetext could be found globally. Therefore, whichever synonym has the greatest match percentage with the freetext will be selected. This could have two possibilities  if only one intent is found with the highest matching percentage globally, then user will be directly navigated to that option which satisfies the above condition as well (synonyms matching <60% is mandatory). For example, - option 1 has matching percentage of 70% - option 2 has matching percentage of 85% then option 2 will be selected  if two or more intents are found with the highest match percentage globally, then user will be prompted with the option of intents which satisfies the above condition as well (synonyms matching <60% is mandatory). For example, - option 1 has match percentage of 70% - option 2 has match percentage of 70% - option 3 has match percentage of 60% then user will be prompted with "Did you mean option1 or option2"  NOTE: 1. when UseDirectSynonymSearch=0, matching is basically done based on the computation of acceptance value with the freetext. We here refer to it as percentage instead of acceptance value for easy understanding of the concept. question: TMAC Voice Call Transfer - Second agent getting different UCID
answer: When TMAC server transfer or conference a voice call to another agent, the second agent supposed to have the same SessionID as first agent so that all the data in OCM database will have same session Id for all calls.  For voice calls, the TSAPI UCID will be used as the SessionID.  When the 1st agent gets the call from ACD, it gets the UCID in the TSAPI IncomingCall event's "UCID" property as below:  For 1st agent, the SessionID (UCID) will be "09999041281721204215".  When the 1st agent transfer or conference the call (consult or blind) to another agent, TMAC updates the "UUI" of the call by injecting a "T" (for transfer) and "C" (for conference) into UUI. This injection is done based on the "uui.config" file properties:  TrasnferUUI_TC_Start = 56 TrasnferUUI_TC_Len = 1 This config means, the transfer/conference flag character (T or C) is inserted into 56th position of the UUI.  After modifying the UUI, then TMAC calls "TransferCall" TSAPI methods. This will initiate a new call to second agent and the second agent will receive an "IncomingCall" TSAPI event as below:  TMAC server reads the incoming event's UUI and check if there is a "T" or a "C" in 56th position of the UUI (based on uui.config file).  If it finds the "T" or the "C", then it looks for the property "OrigUCID". If the "OrigUCID" is present, then TMAC will use that value as the UCID and disregard the "UCID". So the SessionID for the second agent will be "OrigUCID".  At the same time, TMAC will use "OrigCallingDevice" as the phone number.  Potential Issues:  If the second agent is getting a different UCID, it can happen due to several reasons.  The uui.config does not have the config to inject "T" or "C" flag - if this is the case, then the second agent does not have a way to identify the call as a transfered/conferenced call and read OrigUCID. So it will use the "UCID" as SessionID.  The uui.config has some invalid setting causing "T" or "C" to shift to different location in UUI - second agent expects the "T" or "C" flag to be in the position configured in uui.conf. The below config in uui.conf will shift the flag by 19 characters because the actual UCID length is 20 but the config is expecting it to be 1. You can fix it by setting "TransferUUI_OrigUCID_Len" to "20" which is actual UCID length.  TransferUUI_OrigUCID_Len = 1 TransferUUI_OrigUCID_Start = 0 Second agent not getting OrigUCID - due to some issues at AES/TSAPI, there is a chance of TMAC not getting the OrigUCID property in incoming call event. If that happens, the second agent will use the "UCID" as sessionID.  This can happen if the IVR call transfer to queue/agent was done to a "hunt number" rather than a "vdn number". In IVR, the agent transfer vdn should always be a "VDN" so that we can have a vector step to queue the call to relevant skill. If the transfer vdn is the hunt number (or skill extension), then TMAC may not get correct OrigUCID.

question: SMSAPI - what is the usage of ConsiderAgentIdAsSkill config in smsapi
answer: Agents can have multiple skills. Tetherfi WorkQueue assigns items to agents based on these skills.  If the WQ wants to assign an item to a particular agent and that agent only (direct agent routing-DAC), then we have to create a dedicated skill for the agent and route the item to that skill.  Creating dedicated skills for each and every agent will require lot of work on OCM skill configuration module. So, TMAC/SMS API has added this feature to consider the Agent ID as a skill for the agent. So, along with all the skills configured in OCM (or in CM), the AgentID also becomes another skill for the agent. And if some component (like TCamp, TPPVA) add an item to WQ with skill as an AgentID, it will get routed to that particular agent.  The configuration "ConsiderAgentIdAsSkill" enables this feature.

question: VIVR - Livechat1 - Why does the Open() request fail with RequestFailed
answer: The livechat1 SDK "Open" method opens a new session with TComm Http Proxy. After "Open", the proxy excepts a "Start" command to start the session. When the "Start" happens, the Proxy connects with TComm Server and create a new interaction.  After receiving an "Open", the Comm Http Proxy waits for "Start" and if the "Start" did not receive within the "Session timeout" configured value in proxy config, the proxy terminates and removes the session from the TComm Http Proxy. However, there is no event sent back to the livechat1 SDK when this removal happens because there is no DWR (long polling) channel has been established between the UI and proxy yet.  So, the UI may not know about the session getting removed from the server and try to call "Start" which will result in a "session not open" error.  To avoid this, the Visual IVR product implements a timeout that ends the session after N number of seconds after the open, if the "Start" was not called. This ensure the proxy does not end the session and the UI always ends the session so that UI knows about the termination.

question: Tetherfi Work Assignment - Skill Level vs Skill Priority
answer: Skill Priority  Skill Priority is a feature of WorkQueue. Each skill in the WQ (TMAC_Skill table) can be given a priority (low, medium, high). If a priority is not specified, the skill will be considered a “medium” priority by default.  For example, the TMAC_Skills table can have below skills with different priorities:  WorkQueue keeps reading this TMAC_Skills table every 5 minutes to keep the priority details in sync in workqueue memory.  During WQ item processing, it keeps three logical queues for items assigned with high, medium, and low priority skills. WQ starts its processing with items in high priority skills, followed by medium and low. So, if we have two items in WQ with a high priority skill and a low priority skill, the item with high priority skill will be routed regardless of its time of adding to the queue. See below example:  There were seven items added to the queue and there was no agent logged in, so all the items were in the queue.  At 10:40 a.m., an agent with all three skills (40001, 40002, 40003) logged into TMAC. Then routing started. The order of routing is mentioned in the last column.  Skill Level (Proficiency)  Skill Level is a value between 1 to 16 that is assigned to an agent along with a skill. Whenever we assign a skill to an agent, we have to set a skill level as well. The default skill level is set to 1.  Skill level is used during routing to choose the best agent when we have two agents eligible to receive an item.  For example, see below data:  Here we have two agents having skill 40001 but with two different skill levels.  If both the agents logged in at the same time, and was idle for similar about of time, both of them are eligible to receive the next item that comes to queue with skill 40001.  So, WQ uses the skill level to decide which agent should be receiving the item. In above example, agent 50001 receives the item because he/she has a strong skill level (1) than agent 50002 (skill level 2).  In other words, the skill level indicates that agent 50001 is proficient handling calls/chat coming to skill 40001 than agent 50002.  Note:  Please note that there are several configurations in WQ to make skill priority and skill level work properly. Please refer to Tetherfi > Products > WorkQueue > Design Document — Folderit

question: Skill dashboard in AD gets data from which component
answer: Agent Desktops Skill Dashboard (or Wallboard) in the Home screen gets data from TMAC server's WallboardRefreshEvent.  When agent login to TMAC server, it will call SMS API to get agent's skills. Based on SMS API's config, the skills will be coming from Avaya CM or TMAC_Agent_Skills table.  After getting the skills, TMAC will try to get the status of the skill. Status means the Available and Staffed agent count, and the calls in queue (CIQ) count. If the Agent is logged into Avaya CM, TMAC gets these data from Avaya by calling TSAPI methods (getQueueStatus). If the agent is logged into TMAC only (dummy login), then TMAC gets the data from TMAC memory.  After getting the skill list for the agent from SMS API and skill status from TSAPI or TMAC memory, it sends a WalllboardRefreshEvent to AD UI, and UI shows the Skill Dashboard.  If you are not seeing the dashboard, there can be several reasons:  Agent does not have any skills in CM or in TMAC_Agent_Skills (OCM)  TMAC to SMS API connection has a problem.  SMS API to Database connection has a problem (if skill source is Database)  SMS API to AES connection has a problem (if skill source is CM)  Also, if AD to TMAC server event socket (or GetEvent polling) is not happening, then the WallboardRefreshEvent will not be received to AD. But, if events are not working, then most of the AD features will not work (such as receiving and incoming call).

question: How to Enable deflect to digital in TPPVA?
answer: You can configure deflect to digital widget in Agent desktop. Refer - Agent Desktop widget configurations  https://dice.tetherfi.cloud/agent-desktop-docs/modules.html#TwDeflectToDigital  TPPVA Configuration should be enabled according to the requirement.  "DeflectCheckEnabled": "1", "Deflect_ValidAgentState": "Available", "Deflect_UseIwBeforeDeflect": "1", "Deflect_DropChatWhenDeflectFailed": "1", "Deflect_MaxUsagePerUrl": 0, DeflectCheckEnabled - When set to 1, TPPVA will perform the deflect check for all incoming chats.  Deflect_ValidAgentState - When a deflected vivr call comes to TPPVA, and TPPVA wants to route it to agent based on deflect data, it has to first check the agent status. If the agent status is listed in this config (comma separated), then TPPVA can route. Else, it will set a variable "deflect_state" with value "invalid_agent_state" that can be handled further in IW.  Deflect_UseIwBeforeDeflect - When set to 1, TPPVA pass the control back to IW after performing all deflect steps. So, IW can add further logic. TPPVA will not route to agent when we have this config enabled. It expects IW to do that based on the variables set.  Deflect_DropChatWhenDeflectFailed - When "Deflect_UseIwBeforeDeflect=0" and the deflect process fails due to some reason (like DB read failure), TPPVA will disconnect the chat. question: What are the logout reason codes used in TMAC?
answer: AgentStatusCheckTimerElapsed - When there is no communication from UI to the server for a specific time period (AgentConnectionTimeout config in template.conf), TMAC server will remove the agent session with this reason code.  StationNotRegistered - After successful login, if the “AgentLogin_CheckStationValidity” config is set to 1 in the TMAC template config, TMAC checks if the Avaya station is logged in (and registered) to CM/SM. This is done by calling from the station to a VDN (AgentLogin_CheckStationValidityNumber config). If this call fails, then TMAC logs out of the agent session with this reason code.  OnServerStop - If TMAC config “AgentSession_NoLogoutOnStop” is set to “0", TMAC will log off all the agents when TMAC service is stopped with this reason code.  AgentNotLoggedIn-RemoveSession - During an agent login process, TMAC checks if an existing session is already available for the same agent ID and station ID. If it is available, then TMAC checks if that agent is logged into Avaya CM with same agent ID. If there is no login found in CM, then TMAC removes the existing session with this reason code.  AgentNotInAcd-RemoveSession - During the agent login process, TMAC checks if there is an existing session using the same station ID. If there is an existing session with the same station ID, then TMAC checks if that station ID is still logged in (ACD) with some agent ID. If the station is not logged into Avaya CM, then TMAC logoff the existing session with this reason code.  ManualLogout - The logout command is called from the UI (via TMAC proxy).  ManualLogout: <reason> - UI called the logout with a reason code (via TMAC proxy)  Manage_RemoveAgentSession - Agent session removed from a management app (such as TMC) by calling TMAC method “Manage_RemoveAgentSession”.  AgentMoved - When an agent is moved from one TMAC to another (suing a tool such as TMC), the first TMAC has to perform a soft logout to delete the session from TMAC memory. TMAC does that with this reason code.  Unknown - The logout reason code is updated in the table during agent logout. For some reason (such as DB failure), if this logout reason does not get updated during the agent logout, then TMAC will update the record with reason code "Unknown" whenever the same agent login to TMAC again.

question: How does the file transfer between VIVR and Agent Desktop works?
answer: During a chat conversation, the customer and agent are required to exchange files. These files can be images or documents.  When using VIVR at client side and Agent Desktop for agent, the below mechanism is used for sharing files between each other.  The Tetherfi Chat solution has two different ways of sharing files. One with ApiFileUploadDownload (Media Proxy) and other way is using File Streamer and File Uploader.  The ApiFileUploadDownload (Media Proxy) is deprecated and should not be used anymore. In this article, we will only discuss the File Streamer and File Uploader.  Product Components used:  Visual IVR  TComm Proxy  TComm Server  TMAC Proxy  TMAC Server  Agent Desktop  File Uploader  File Streamer  Configurations  TComm Proxy:  Configure the file streamer and file uploader in Tcomm proxy config:  https://tetherfi.cloud/api/proxyconfig.jsp  File Download URL - File streamer (https://dev.tetherfi.cloud:13022)  File Upload Path - File Uploader URL (https://dev.tetherfi.cloud:13019/upload)  VIVR Config:  "CommunicationInterface": { "livechat1": { "enabled": true, "mediaStreamer": { "enable": true, "organizationId": "Tetherfi", "uploader": "Dicedev" } } } In VIVR config, we have to set “mediaStreamer” enabled to true.  AD Config->Default.json  "Urls": { "FileServerUrl": { "MediaUploader": "https://dev.tetherfi.cloud:13019/upload", "MediaStreamer": "https://dev.tetherfi.cloud:13022", "MediaProxy": "https://dev.tetherfi.cloud/ApiFileUploadDownLoad" } } Customer sending file to agent:  In VIVR, customer can upload a file during self service (form nodes), or during a live chat with agent.  Whenever customer select a file/image to upload, VIVR calls livechat SDK method “uploadFiles” to send the file to TcommProxy.  After TcommProxy gets the file, it calls the File Uploader URL to upload the file to File Uploader.  Based on the configuration of File Uploader, it will either save the file to local file system, or to S3.  After that, File Uploader will return back the details on how to download the file via File Streamer. This data will have a downloadUrl (with a unique ID).  TComm proxy returns this response to VIVR via livechat SDK (OnUploadComplete event)  VIVR gets the file download url details from “OnUploadComplete” event, and then sends it to Agent Desktop as a message.  The message goes to TCommProxy to TcommServer, to TMAC to Agent Desktop.  After receiving the message, Agent Desktop understands it is a file coming from VIVR which was uploaded to File Uploader. For that Agent Desktop uses the “uploader” property of incoming message in TextChatMessageReceivedEvent. The value of “uploader” property “MediaStreamer” means the VIVR has uploaded the file via File Streamer. The “src” property of the message has the “interaction id” of the attachment.  Agent desktop has to form the File Streamer URL using config and above “src” property.  Urls.FilerServerUrl.MediaStreamer/stream/media/<src>  Then AD will download the file via File Streamer using above url.  Agent Sending File to customer:  If the config “Urls.FilerServerUrl.MediaUploader” is defined in default.json, then AD will use the File Uploader the upload files.  When the agent select a file, it will be uploaded and the “interaction_id” for each file is preserved in AD UI memory.  After uploading is done, then a JSON message from AD to VIVR is sent with downloadUrl (the downloadUrl is returned by File Uploader during upload).  When VIVR receives the message, it will request TComm Proxy to download the file.  Related links:  tmac server- what is the usage of 'FileserverURL' config key

question: tmacserver-what is the difference between Voice_OriginatedNumberModifyRules and Voice_OutboundNumberModifyRules config keys
answer: Voice_OutboundNumberModifyRules  <add key="Voice_OutboundNumberModifyRules" value="^(\+60).{10,}$:trim=3,trimend=2,prefix=9,suffix=;^(\+65).{8,}$:trim=3,prefix=9;^.{8}$:prefix=9,replace=" />  This key is used for updating the outbound (called) number. For example, if the agent enters "+6596975347" for Make Call, then TMAC can update this "+6596975347" to a different number and dial out. For example, TMAC can remove "+65" and add a "prefix 9" to the number before sending the call to PBX/CM. So the number dialed by TMAC will be "996975347".  The config can have multiple "sets". Each set is separated by a semi-colon ";".  Set 1 - "^(\+60).{10,}$:trim=3,trimend=2,prefix=9,suffix="  Set 2 - "^(\+65).{8,}$:trim=3,prefix=9;^.{8}$:prefix=9"  Each "set" has two parts separated by colon ":".  The left part is a "regular expression/Regex" and the right part is a set of actions.  Set 1 Regex - "^(\+60).{10,}$" - check if the number starts with +60 and has 10 digits after that.  Set 2 Regex - "^(\+65).{8,}$" - checks if the number starts with +65 and has 8 digits after that.  Regex:  The regex is used for validating the number entered by the agent. In this example, regex will check if the number starts with "+65" and has eight digits ("96975347" - Singapore local number) after that.  Actions:  Once the Regex matches, the actions specifies what should be done to the phone number.  There are several types of actions:  "trim=3" - trims 3 digits from the start of the number.  "trimend=2" - trims 2 digits from the end of the number.  "prefix=9" - adds a prefix "9" to the start of the number  "suffix=9" - adds a suffix 9 to the end of the number.  Voice_SourceNumberModifyRules  This config is used only when agent is logged into "Webphone" and the Media Server connects to a SIP PBX.  When agent dials and outbound call, the original from number will have agent's stationid. TMAC will update the "from" number before sending the call to media server. So the media server will send the same "from" number in the SIP INVITE "from" field to the SIP PBX. If the SIP PBX allows "source number" modifications, the customer will see the this updated number as the calling party.  The configuration (regex and actions) is same as "Voice_OutboundNumberModifyRules" above. However, there is an extra "action":  "replace=123456" - the whole "from" number will be replaced with "123456". So the customer will see CLI as "123456" instead of agent's station number.  Voice_OriginatedNumberModifyRules  This configuration is used when agent is logged into Avaya/Cisco CTI or Media Server. Based on this config TMAC changes the destination phone number that will be displayed to the agent on TMAC UI/Agent Desktop. Also TMAC uses this updated phone number when saving data to databases and logs. The actual number send to Avaya/Cisco/MediaServer is NOT altered here.  The configuration is same as "Voice_SourceNumberModifyRules"  For example, if the agent dials "96975347", TMAC can change that to "+65969753467" to be displayed to agent UI. This data is sent to UI in "OutgoingCallEvent.PhoneNumber" property.  The main usecase of this configuration would be number masking on data reports. If there are certain number patterns that should not be saved to the data tables directly, then we can use this config to mask those numbers.

In IW Agent Node, there is a configuration for survey variables.  When TPPVA transfers the call to a live agent, these survey variables are sent to TMAC as part of UserJsonData "param5". This has to be enabled in TPPVA to send param5. See How do I configure TPPVA and TMAC server to pass user data from TPPVA to TMAC for ReQueue?  When the live agent ends the chat by clicking the end button on the UI, the TMAC server processes the below logic to see if a chat survey is needed.  Check if "TextChat_TransferOnEnd" is set to 1. If set to '0', then no survey is offered.  Check if "TextChat_TransferOnEndSkill" has a value. This value should have the TPPVA skill. If there is no value given, then the survey is not offered.  Check the value of "TextChat_TransferOnEndType". This variable can have two different values.  "transfer" - TMAC does a blind transfer to TPPVA skill  "requeue" - TMAC requeues the chat back to TPPVA skill. This is the recommended and preferred setting for survey to work properly.  If the "TextChat_TransferOnEndType=requeue", then TMAC server will check the data which came from "param5".  If "param5.enableSurvey" is set to true (this comes from TPPVA based on IW Agent Node), then TMAC goes to next step  If "param5.surveyIntent" is set then TMAC uses that as the survey intent, else it uses the value configured in "TextChat_TransferOnEndIntent" TMAC config  When all above steps are passed, then TMAC set the ReQueue value to "TextChat_TransferOnEndSkill" from TMAC config  Then TMAC calls "ReQueue" method of TComm Server to Requeue the chat to TPPVA skill  TPPVA receives the chat with Survey Intent and then executes the survey flow.

question: TMAC Server- need details on 'TextChat_BlindTransferCheckQStatus' config key

question: tmac server- what is functionality of 'GenericInterationStartupCount' config key
answer: TMAC Server has an interaction type called "generic interaction". Generic Interactions are those interactions which does not below to voice, chat, email, fax, or social media. question: AgentStatusCheckTimerElapsed
answer: When TMAC Client or Agent Desktop login to TMAC server, the client starts a GetEvent connection with server. This connection can be either a polling connection (request/response in periodic manner) or a SignalR (Websocket) connection.  This connection is made from client to server immediately after a successful login.  Then TMAC server starts a thread to keep checking if the client is active. TMAC checks this in two different ways for polling and SignalR connections:  Polling - If polling connection is used, TMAC server treats the connection as active if UI calls the "GetEvent" polling method.  SignalR - If signalR connection is used, TMAC server treats the connection as active if UI sends "ping" message over SignalR connection.  TMAC server has a configuration called "AgentConnectionTimeout".  If the TMAC server does not get a "GetEvent" request or a "ping" message from the UI for a period of time specified in "AgentConnectionTimeout", TMAC server assumes that the UI is not there anymore.  It may be due to the UI is closed, or the network between the UI and the server is disconnected, or the UI is frozen due to resource unavailability. Also, it may happen if the UI has some custom codes added to show a "modal" popup which blocks it from calling TMAC GetEvent method.  Once TMAC detects that UI is not active anymore, TMAC decides to log the agent out with reason code as "AgentStatusCheckTimerElapsed".  So, if we see logout code as "AgentStatusCheckTimerElapsed", it means the UI to TMAC server communication has broken.

question: LimitCallFACRules key in TMACServer
answer: LimitCall is a feature provided by Avaya CM. It limits the number of calls that can be handled by an Avaya station. To enable or disable limit calling feature on a station, we can dial an “fac” (feature access code) as configured in Avaya CM.  Each agent station has more than one lines. It means, agent can receive more than one call. Even for ACD calls, it is possible to receive more than one call if MCH (Multi Call Handling) is enabled in Avaya CM Skills.  When TMAC operates with Avaya TSAPI for Voice and TextChat, TMAC makes use of this feature.  Agents can answer only one voice call at a time. However, agents should be able to answer more than one text chat at a time. To achieve this, Avaya CM’s text chat skills are configured to be MCH (forced).  So, when agent is handling one textchat, agent may receive another textchat from a MCH skill.  However, if the agent is handling a voice call, agent may still receive a text chat call from MCH skill. But, agent cannot answer the text chat because agent has to put the voice call on hold for that.  To handle this situation, TMAC uses the LimitCall feature.  When configured correctly, TMAC calls the LimitCall FAC to limit the calls for that agent’s station whenever TMAC gets a voice call.  incoming call to TMAC  Check limit call configuration  Check auto answer configuration  If auto answer not set, then dial limit call  If auto answer is set, then dial limit call, and when its completed, then perform auto answer  During incoming call, when dialing limit call, there is no need Hold the call line  If the limit call during incoming call fails, TMAC can retry limit call during "on connect" event based on LimitCallsRetryOnConnectEnabled key.  Once limit call is enabled on the station, no other ACD calls (even MCH calls) can be delivered to the same station so that the agent can complete the voice call without disruptions.  Once TMAC enables limit calling for a voice call, it should make sure that limit calls are disabled so that it can receive more than one text chat call. This is done whenever TMAC gets a text chat call. After agent finishes the voice call, Avaya ACD may route a text chat call waiting in the queue to TMAC. When TMAC gets the chat call, and if the configs are enabled, TMAC calls Limit Call disable FAC to disable limit calls. This will allow the CM ACD to route more text chat calls (MCH) to agents. In a text chat interaction, the limit call disable fac is done during “OnConnect” TSAPI event. If all configs are matching, TMAC will HOLD the text chat call (TSAPI Hold), and then dial the fac to disable limit calls.  Configurations:  LimitCallsOnACDVoiceCall – when set to 1, TMAC will consider calling fac to enable limit calls for ACD voice calls.  LimitCallsOnAllIncomingVoiceCall – when set to 1, TMAC will consider calling fac to enable limit calls for all voice calls.  LimitCallEnableFacNumber – fac to enable limit calls (to be configured in Avaya CM)  LimitCallDisableFacNumber - fac to disable limit calls (to be configured in Avaya CM)  LimitCallFACRules – if LimitCallsOnACDVoiceCall or LimitCallsOnAllIncomingVoiceCall is set to 1, then TMAC checks LimitCallFACRules.  LimitCallFACRules is a written as a SQL statement which will return “true” or “false”. Below paramerts are passed to the rule:  "0" – TotalTabsAllowed (in agent profile)  "1" – TotalVoiceTabsAllowed (in agent profile)  "2" -  TotalChatTabsAllowed (in agent profile)  Other values that can be used:  none – do not apply rules  all – apply for all calls  Example:  LimitCallFACRules = "{0}!=1 and {2}!=10"  Means --> "TotalTabsAllowed != 1 AND TotalChatTabsAllowed != 10"  LimitCallsRetryOnConnectEnabled  This config "LimitCallsRetryOnConnectEnabled" is used for retrying a limit call fac in case the original one failed. Another limit call is tried after TMAC gets a connected event.  Caution:  If LimitCalls are enabled, it is mandatory to ensure that correct LimitCallEnableFacNumber and LimitCallDisableFacNumber are configured. A wrong number configured will result in a "OnFailed" event and may cause Voice and Chat interaction states to behave unexpectedly.

question: Why do we need to set LoadUserProfile as True in OCM application pool
answer: In .NET 6 and previous versions, when hosting an application in Internet Information Services (IIS), you may need to set the LoadUserProfile property to true in the application pool configuration. This setting ensures that the user profile associated with the application pool identity is loaded when the application starts.  Here are a few reasons why this setting is necessary:  Access to user-specific resources: When an application runs under a specific user identity, such as a domain account, it may need access to user-specific resources such as the user's profile folder, registry settings, or user-specific configuration files. Loading the user profile ensures that these resources are available to the application.  Configuration settings: Some applications rely on configuration settings stored in the user's profile, such as custom environment variables or user-specific settings files. By loading the user profile, the application can access and utilize these configuration settings.  User-specific permissions: The user profile contains various permissions and access rights specific to the user. Certain applications may require these permissions to function correctly. By loading the user profile, the application can inherit the necessary permissions associated with the user.  Application dependencies: Some applications rely on libraries or components that require access to user-specific resources or configurations. By loading the user profile, the application ensures that these dependencies can function properly.  It's important to note that not all applications require the LoadUserProfile property to be set to true. If your application doesn't rely on user-specific resources or configurations, or if it runs under a system account that doesn't have a user profile, then setting LoadUserProfile to true may not be necessary.  However, if your application does require access to user-specific resources or configurations, it's recommended to set LoadUserProfile to true in the application pool configuration to ensure the application functions as intended.  In OCM logs you could see below errors   2023-05-05 18:39:00,389 [.NET ThreadPool Worker] DEBUG OCM.Controllers.ErrorController -Access to the path 'C:\Windows\TEMP\ASPNETCORE_99f4d3a1-807d-49f5-ac71-437beef12122.tmp' is denied.: 2023-05-05 18:39:00,389 [.NET ThreadPool Worker] DEBUG OCM.Controllers.ErrorController - Microsoft.Win32.SafeHandles.SafeFileHandle CreateFile(System.String, System.IO.FileMode, System.IO.FileAccess, System.IO.FileShare, System.IO.FileOptions): 2023-05-05 18:39:00,389 [.NET ThreadPool Worker] DEBUG OCM.Controllers.ErrorController - Internal server error: The reason for this is that LoadUserProfile is not loaded, which affects environment variables such as %TEMP% and others.

question: How does the Event Delivery between TMAC Client and TMAC Server works?
answer: Event Delivery between TMAC Client and TMAC Server  TMAC server and TMAC Client communicates with each other using commands and events. Commands are sent from the client to server and events are sent from the server to client.  For the client to send commands to the server, it can use a HTTP request that goes from client to TMAC proxy, and then from TMAC proxy to TMAC server.  However, for the server to send events to client, there is no established connection between the server and client.  To address this challenge, the TMAC client and TMAC server implements several event delivery mechanisms.  When we develop a TMAC UI/Agent Desktop UI using TMAC SDK (JavaScript), the SDK implements these mechanisms in the sdk so that the UI does not have to worry about the implementation.  Ajax polling / short polling  In ajax polling (or short polling), the TMAC client calls a “getevent” method of TMAC proxy. The TMAC proxy then calls the “getevent” method of TMAC server. TMAC server checks if there are any events for that agent session in the event queue. If available, then the events are returned back to UI. If no events available, then an empty response is returned to UI.  Upon receiving the response from TMAC server, the UI (SDK), waits for 500 milliseconds and calls “getevent” again.  There are some drawbacks of Ajax polling. When there are large number of agents (let’s say 500 agents), polling for events via the TMAC proxy, the proxy will get about 1000 requests per second. Also, the TMAC server also gets about 1000 request per seconds which may cause TMAC proxy and TMAC server to be overloaded. So, using ajax polling or short polling is not recommended.  SignalR (websocket)  To handle the drawbacks of Ajax polling, a new method “SignalR” was implemented. SignalR uses a “websocket” between the UI and the server to maintain a persistent connection.  When a new agent login to the TMAC server by calling the Login method in SDK, the TMAC server returns a SignalR url of that TMAC server allowing the SDK (UI) to directly connect to the web socket bypassing the proxy. After it is connected, TMAC server keeps sending events related to that agent session whenever an event is generated.  Compared to ajax polling mechanism, the SignalR event delivery is faster and lighter because it pushes events from the server to UI immediately when the events are generated. Also it does not overload the proxy or TMAC server’s HTTP interface.  However, even SignalR can face challenges with unstable networks which has regular disruptions. When a network failure between the UI and the server occurs, the SDK tries to re-initiate the websocket connections. However, regular and lengthy network disconnects may result in reconnect failures.  If the reconnect fails, the SDK has to fallback to another mechanism (ajax polling or long polling).  Long Polling  Long polling was implemented on top of ajax polling by adding a “wait” at the server side. When the UI calls the “getevent” method in TMAC server, the server returns immediately if there were events available in the queue for that agent session. However, if there were no events, TMAC server will wait for 30 seconds (configurable in TMAC config) waiting for events to be added to queue. If any event is added, it would return immediately and the UI would call “getevent” again after 500 ms. If there were no events for 30 seconds, then TMAC would return empty return and the UI would call “getevent” after 500 ms.  With long polling, the HTTP overload of TMAC Proxy and TMAC server is reduced.  Recommendation:  When configuring event delivery, below are the recommendations:  Configure SignalR as primary method  Use long polling as fallback  Do not use ajax polling

question: TMAC Server SignalR Operations
answer: Here is how Agent Desktop and TMAC uses SignalR for Event delivery:  How Agent Desktop + TMAC SignalR works  When the TMAC server starts, it creates a SignalR listener.  Agent Desktop sends the Login command to the TMAC server via TMAC Proxy.  TMAC server responds with its SignalR URL.  Agent Desktop receives the SignalR URL.  Agent Desktop tries to connect to SignalR URL using JQuery SignalR Framework.  The SignalR connection gets created using a “WebSocket”  After connecting, Agent Desktop sends a “connect” command to the TMAC server via the SignalR channel, which was established in previous step. This “connect” command contains the agent identification data so that the TMAC server can associate the SignalR connection to the agent session.  TMAC continues to send agent and interaction events to Agent Desktop over the connected channel.  Agent Desktop keep sending a “ping” message to the TMAC server every 30 seconds. When the TMAC server receives this “ping,” it immediately responds with a “pong”.  References: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/signalr/overview/guide-to-the-api/handling-connection-lifetime-events  https://docs.google.com/document/d/1FfhW3d4WDYUhpr1ZQ9lOxpR-3y8m_jy1nZl4qlx1F2I/edit

question: How does SignalR to GetEvent fallback works in Agent Desktop?
answer: How Agent Desktop + TMAC SignalR works (current implementation)  When the TMAC server starts, it creates a SignalR listener.  Agent Desktop sends the Login command to the TMAC server via TMAC Proxy.  TMAC server responds with its SignalR URL.  Agent Desktop receives the SignalR URL.  Agent Desktop tries to connect to SignalR URL using JQuery SignalR Framework.  The SignalR connection gets created using a “WebSocket”  After connecting, Agent Desktop sends a “connect” command to the TMAC server via the SignalR channel, which was established. This “connect” command contains the agent identification data so that the TMAC server can associate the SignalR connection to the agent session.  TMAC continues to send agent and interaction events to Agent Desktop over the connected channel.  Agent Desktop keep sending a “ping” message to the TMAC server every 30 seconds. When the TMAC server receives this “ping,” it immediately responds with a “pong”.  How Agent Desktop handles the SignalR disconnect  Agent Desktop widget JSON has a configuration for “timeout” (let’s say it is 10 seconds)  When SignalR detects that it is not able to communicate with the TMAC server over the channel, it goes to the “connection slow” state (SignalRConnectionSlowEvent)  Connection Slow happens immediately after SignalR JQeury framework detects there is a communication issue in the channel  Connection Slow event is emitted to Agent Desktop  After sending the Connection Slow event, SignalR JQuery framework starts trying to “reconnect”.  It tries to “reconnect” until the above given “timeout’ (10 seconds in this case) occurs.  If it can “reconnect” within 10 seconds, then Agent Desktop will continue to work on SignalR  If it cannot “reconnect” within 10 seconds, Agent Desktop TMAC SDK will get a SignalRErrorEvent (and a SignalRDisconnected event)  TMAC SDK checks if the “fallback” is enabled.  If fallback is enabled - TMAC SDK calls TMAC Proxy to check if the connected TMAC server is still there.  TMAC Proxy tries to connect to the TMAC server, and if it is there, TMAC proxy returns back to SDK  SDK will now fallback to GetEvent polling  TMAC server will now remove the SignalR connection reference from Agent Session  If TMAC proxy finds the TMAC server is not there, then TMAC proxy login the agent into another TMAC server available.  After login, the Proxy returns the new TMAC server details (SignalR URL) to SDK.  SDK connects to new TMAC server SignalR url  If “fallback” is disabled, the TMAC SDK will keep trying to “connect” (please note this is not “reconnect”) to SignalR URL again.  These reconnect are done in 1, 2,3, 4,... seconds subsequently.  When trying to connect, if the connection is successful, then SDK will send the “connect” command and continue to receive events from TMAC  When trying to connect, if the connection fails, it will try again to connect after t+1 seconds.  If “fallback” is disabled, and if the connected TMAC server crashes, Agent Desktop won't be able to connect to the next available TMAC server (Before TMAC 6.x - Some 5.x versions are patched to fix this)  SignalR documents  Understanding and Handling Connection Lifetime Events in SignalR | Microsoft Learn

question: In Agent desktop, when chat is received by the agent, customer and bot interaction is not available. What are the configurations to be updated?
answer: When TPPVA ReQueue (transfer to liveagent) the chat,there are two ways it can handle the chatbot history.  1) Using Cache (TCache) When TPPVA config "SaveHistoryToCache" is set to "1", it writes the bot history to TCache with below details:  Cache Key = "BOTHISTORY:<sessionid>"  Cache Value = Json Serialized History (see Appendix A below for history structure)  After saving data into Cache, TPPVA calls ReQueue with below value in "history" section of User Json Data:  "FROMCACHE:BOTHISTORY:<sessionid>"  For this mode to work, TPPVA and TMAC should have the TCache configurations.  TPPVA - "DataCacheUrl"  TMAC - "TCacheManager_ConfigJsonPath"  2) Using ReQueue message: When "SaveHistoryToCache" is set to "0", TPPVA writes the serialized history directly to ReQueue message (see Appendix A below for history structure).  How is it Handled in TMAC: When live agent gets the chat (in TMAC server), upon successful bridging, TMAC receives the "RemoteUserConnected" event which will contain the "history" which was saved from TPPVA based on TPPVA config "SaveHistoryToCache".  TMAC checks the history value, and if it starts with "FROMCACHE:", then TMAC reads the history from TCache.  Otherwise, TMAC extracts history directly from the messages came in RemoteUserConnected event.  Once TMAC has the history, it is added to "TextChatRemoteUserConnectedEvent.ChatHistoryData" property and sent to Agent Desktop UI as an event.  Appendix A:  History structure:  public List<MessageHistory> History { get; set; } public class MessageHistory { public string timestamp { get; set; } public string customer_input { get; set; } public string reply { get; set; }  public bool is_tppva { get; set; } }

question: How does TMAC SDK Proxy select TMAC Server from a list when service discovery enabled?
answer: When a Login command is received:  Get the TMAC server address list from Service Registry.  Connect to each TMAC server and collect agent session information (calling GetAgentSessionsInfo method in TMAC server).  Iterate each TMAC server session information received in last step and check if this agent session is active in any of the TMAC servers.  If the session is found in any TMAC server, then use that TMAC server to log in.  If the session is not found in any TMAC server, then proceed to below steps.  Check if any of the TMAC server has reached the capacity (based on the MaxAllowedSessionCount config in the TMAC server and the current session count)  If the session count has reached MaxAllowedSessionCount, then that TMAC server is not considered for login.  After the above operation, we will have several TMAC servers eligible to accept a new login.  Order the server list based on the session count and use the server with the lowest session count to log in.  So, when Service Discovery is enabled, the CapacityRatio and TmacTrySequence configurations are not considered. TMAC proxy always sends the login to the TMAC server with the lowest active session count.

question: What is BOT Conference in Agent Desktop? How does it work?
answer: When a customer connects to an agent via VIVR, the agent has the option to send the customer back to VIVR for secure data collection. This is almost similar to a Voice call getting transferred/Conferenced to IVR for TPIN/OTP validation.  Agent desktop has a feature called BOT conference (in the conference dialog) to conference the customer back to the TPPVA agent.  First, the agent has to select the BOT conference intent (which comes from the IW intent list) and after that agent can initiate the conference.  TMAC server will create a conference with the TPPVA agent. When the TPPVA agent gets the conference chat, it will execute the IW flow for the selected intent.  All the messages between the customer and TPPVA agent will be masked to the live agent in Agent desktop.  The IW flow can have menus, forms, modules etc, to perform the required operations. At the end of the flow, there should be a "disconnect" node.  When TPPVA finds the "disconnect" node, it will disconnect the TPPVA agent from the conference and the customer and agent will be back to one-to-one interaction.  The below setting in VIVR has to be enabled for this feature to work fine: ChatbotSelfServiceEndedRoutingEnabled  Agent Desktop gets the list of bot conference endpoints from TMAC Server. TMAC server gets this list from IW by calling "GetDnisFlowMap" endpoint.  TMAC config for this looks like below:  <add key="Data_TextChatSelfServiceLoadIwUrls" value="http://dice.tetherfi.cloud:9802/IWInterpreterWebApp/restServices/GetDnisFlowMap" />  When a bot is conferenced, the messages between the bot and customer will not be visible to agent. For example, the user might be entering the credit card details to bot's flow and that should not be shown to agent. Agent will see a generic message "message from bot" or "message from customer" just to be aware that the communication is going on.

question: How to determine OCM ReportScheduler HA mode, active-active or active-passive?

question: How does the text chat auto response works in text chat?
answer: Customer sends a messages.  Then agent can respond.  After agent response, TMAC starts a timer and wait for customer to respond.  To wait for customer message, TMAC has to start a timer. This timer's time is takes from OCM Chat Templates with name 'AutoTemplate_X' where is the time to wait ( X can be like 30, 60, 90...)  Timer will expire at each X (30, 60, 90...).  When timer expires, TMAC checks if the customer has responded and the timer will stop (while waiting if customer responds, the timer will stop).  If the customer has not responded, then the auto-response message is sent to the customer (for the X value), and timer resests for next X.  If the customer never responds before all the X expires, the timer understand the last X as the final response, and stops the timer after that.

question: When VIVR/Chatbot connects to TComm proxy, it gets an error "UnOpenedSessionNotAllowed". What is the re
answer: There can be two reasons to get this "UnOpenedSessionNotAllowed" error in livechat SDK.  Firstly, the "Session timeout" configuration in TComm Proxy can be a cause for this. If the "Session Timeout" in tcomm proxy is set to 0, or very small value below 5 seconds, then this error will happen.  To rectify, change the session timeout to larger value (120 for example)  The second reason could be due to invalid Load Balancer configuration.  If there are two TComm proxies and the UI connect to tcomm proxy via an LB, the LB should be configured to handle the session stickiness.  If the LB does not perform session stickinness, every alternate request from the UI might goto different TComm proxies and the proxy will return "UnOpenedSessionNotAllowed" error.  In the web browser console (network tab), you can check the JSessionId cookie. If this cookie value keeps chanign for each dwr request, then there is a potential stickiness issue in LB.

For the routing to happen the TPPVA agent should have the right set of Skills,  and the tab count for textchat, video, and audio should be set accordingly.  Also, in WQ the chat routing should allow "On Call" state.  Apart from that, if the channel is video or audio (chat mode in VIVR), then the "GenericRouter_LimitCallChannels" should not have "audio" and "video" in TMAC template.config  Also, in OCM user on boarding, the "AccessRole" for chatbot agent should be set to "chatbot"  If any of the above things are not there, there is a possibility of chatbot answering few chats and then not answer any more chats.  To find out why items not coming to chatbot, you can check the TMAC server's generic router logs. It will show the chatbot agent with state, skills, tab counts and give an indication why the routing is not happening.

question: When does the interaction conversion to generic channel in ekycaudit widget fails?
answer: In Agent Desktop/TMAC, there is a feature to allow converting a TextChat Interaction to a "Generic Interaction".  The convert feature is used in two different cases:  1- To send a eKYC video call to another department for audit  2- To convert a text chat to an async chat  eKYC Audit:  Agent sends a convert command to text chat interaction in TMAC server with "channel=generic", the skill number, and additional data containing the data collected during the video call (such as snapshot images).  Then the TMAC server generates a new WQ item by calling work queue. The work queue items then gets routed to another agent with the skill as an generic interaction. The agent desktop UI handles this generic interaction based on the subchannel specified.  If the convert is failing, we have to look at the error codes.  -100 : Agent is not logged  -1 : Generic failure (refer to TMAC server logs to find out more)  -2 : exception in convert. Check TMAC server logs.  Convert to Async:  TMAC has the ability to convert a live chat to an async chat. When this conversion happens, the chat is re-queued to bot agent (tppva agent) skill and the chat gets transferred to tppva. And the TPPVA handles it as an async chat.

question: What is the use of "Recorder_Ext_StartsWith" and "Recorder_Exts_Range" in TMAC Server
answer: When TMAC uses Avaya TSAPI for CTI, the TMAC server receives Avaya TSAPI events. The TMAC logic to handle calls is developed based on these events.  https://docs.google.com/document/d/12BGVEeIh9VqMWkuEkiyiSsMKAnvGtfyl9syUurm4hGs/edit  For example, when the TMAC receives an “Incoming Call” event, it creates a new Voice or Chat interaction and after answering the call (or auto answer from CM), it gets a “Connect” event which changes the state of the call to “Connected”. In an environment where the telephony is handled by Avaya, for call recording, it uses a technique referred to as “DMCC” recording.
