question: When VIVR connects to TPPVA, it shows as a conference (multiple TPPVA agents connected to VIVR)
answer: This "conference" scenario happens when the same VIVR session gets connected to TPPVA agent twice (as two different interactions for TPPVA agent).  It is an indication that the item was routed to the agent twice by the WQ.  The WQ may route the same item twice in two different scenarios.  The item was added to WQ twice by the TComm Server  WQ ACK is enabled, but there is no ACK received so WQ routes again after the ACK TTL  Item added to WQ Twice:  This can happen if the "call agent" configuration in TCommProxy and TCommServer has a mismatch. When the VIVR connects to TCommProxy using the livechat SDK, the TCommProxy connects to TCommServer and creates a new session. However, the TCommServer does not automatically push the item to WQ. To push the item to WQ, there are two different ways:  TCommServer has a configuration "enable.callagentMsg" - if this value is set to "false", TCommServer will automatically push the item to WQ. If this value is set to "true", then TCommServer waits for further routing instructions from TCommProxy  TCommProxy has a configuration "Auto Call Queue" - if this value is set to "true", then TCommProxy will instruct the TCommServer to push the item to WQ.  Please see below combinations:  So, we have to make sure both these configurations are either set to "TRUE" or "FALSE".  If these values are not properly set, then the item may not get routed or it may get routed twice.  WQ ACK enabled and no ACK from agent:  Sending ACK response to WQ when an items is routed is done in the TMAC UI SDK (JS). So, if any items is routed to any other application which is not TMAC UI (such as TPPVA), it won't get any ACK response.  To handle this scnerio for TPPVA, the WQ and TMAC uses the "Agent Access Role" of TPPVA agent. If the "Access Role" is set to "Chatbot", then WQ does not wait for an ACK response from TPPVA agent. After sending item to TPPVA, the WQ immediately removes the item from the queue.  So, we have to make sure the TPPVA agent's role is set to "Chatbot" in OCM User Onboargin module. This data gets saved into "AGT_TMACAgentProfile" table's "AccessRole" column for the "AgentId".  If these values are not properly set, the item may get routed many times.

question: How Tetherfi WebRTC Recorder Works?
answer: WebRTC Media Server:  The WebRTC Media server connects to the Livechat server and intercepts audio/video (via Internet) call requests. Upon intercepting a request it will create a session for the particular audio/video conversation and request both customer and Agents to connect to Media Server (as opposed to connecting to each other as in the earlier system). The media server relays and audio/video data received by connected parties to the other parties. While relaying the data, the server would save a copy of the raw data to the local cache. The Media server hosts a service for Recorder to connect and retrieve these cached raw data. Upon Recorder’s successful consumption of the data files, these files are removed from the cache.  WebRTC Recorder :  The WebRTC Recorder periodically queries for raw media files of recent audio/video sessions and transfers them to the recording server. Then they are encoded, encapsulate in commonly playable container formats (“webm” or “mp4” file), encrypted using AES keys retrieved from KMS, and archived for later references. Upon successful archival Media Server is notified for it to remove the raw files from its cache. The recording server provides a REST service for OCM and other reporting tools to query such archived files. The REST interface is described below. A “conversation” is the smallest unit that WebRTC Recorder and WebRTC Media Server handle. That is, either Media Server has a complete conversation (i.e. all the raw data related to the conversation) or it does not have a conversation at all. Also, the Recorder may have a completely encoded final conversation (i.e. all the encoded audio/video files of that conversation) or it does not have the conversation at all. A raw conversation data from a Media Server will only be given to a single Recorder for conversion and only one Recorder will be allowed to convert a particular conversation. Thus if multiple recorders have cached the same conversation, they both should be identical. This is implemented by, making sure a chat session only interacts with one Media Server at a time and the Media Server only allows a conversation to be fed to a single Recorder.

question: What is functionality of WebClient and CallSDK Js?
answer: Call SDK is a SDK released by Tetherfi for helping end users create Web based audio/video call applications. This SDK is used by  Internal developers (e.g. VIVR, TComm TestApp, TMAC) to implement audio/video call applications  External developers (e.g. Our customer's development teams, Partners of our customers, and Third party vendors of our customers like VTM vendors) to incorporate Web based audio/video call functionality to their applications.  WebClientAPI is a SDK that provides lower level functionality of audio/video functionality such as handling audio video streams and abstracting various cross browser compatibilities. This SDK is usually only used by Call SDK and is usually not directly used by any other party (apart for some instances due to historical reasons).  Since both of these SDKs are used by application developers to develop other applications (e.g. VIVR), the deployment of these depends on the application in use. Thus ideally, those applications deployment guides should contain instructions on how to deploy/upgrade this dependent library (i.e. Call SDK and WebClient API).  Call SDK Deployment (Generic Guidelines)  The Call SDK general deployment instructions are present in the ReadMe.txt in a Call SDK release archive. Please refer to the same for your release incase they are more up to date than these instructions.  The Call SDK release may contain following 3 archives,  Call SDK Release archive  Usually named in the form livechat_http-with-webclientapi_vVERSION.zip; this archive contains the release build of the Call SDK. It contains 4 files named adapter.js, livechat_video.js, livechat_video.min.js and livechat_video.react.min.js.  The adapter.js contains utility functions to normalize the underlying browser APIs and to provide cross browser compatibility.  The livechat_video.js is provides the Call SDK API and call handling functionality.  The livechat_video.min.js and livechat_video.react.min.js has identical functionality to livechat_video.js and only differ in build mode. livechat_video.min.js is a minified version of livechat_video.js. livechat_video.react.min.js is a special build of livechat_video.js that supports easy integration to React JS framework.  Since livechat_video.js, livechat_video.min.js and livechat_video.react.min.js are identical in functionality, only one of these files are usually deployed in a application. It is recommended to the application developers to use livechat_video.min.js or livechat_video.react.min.js over livechat_video.js in production builds.  Call SDK Debug archive  Web Client API Archive  Asp per current implementations, please find the instructions to deploy this library on VIVR, TMAC and TComm TestApp applications.  Note: Please note that these instructions are only valid for up to the time of writing this article and may change in future; Thus always refer to the deployment guides of the application for the instructions if any.  Deploying Call SDK on VIVR  Out of the two libraries, VIVR only depends on Call SDK. The call SDK files are located in VIVR deployment on following relative path (Assuming VIVR is deployed on Tomcat's webappps\visual-ivr directory).  webapps\visual-ivr\assets\js\adapter.js webapps\visual-ivr\assets\js\livechat_video_debug.js webapps\visual-ivr\assets\js\livechat_video.min.js webapps\visual-ivr\assets\js\livechat_video.js Depending on the VIVR release, one ore more of the livechat_video_debug.js, livechat_video.min.js or livechat_video.js would be present on the above path. Also the adapter.js will be present in the above path.  To update the Call SDK, please extract the new Call SDK release archive and replace the files present in the above directory from the ones in the release archive. You are only to replace the existing files and any additional files in Call SDK release should not be deployed unless explicitly stated in the ReadMe.txt in Call SDK release archive.

question: How do I configure TPPVA and TMAC server to pass user data from TPPVA to TMAC for ReQueue?
answer: When we use TPPVA with VIVR and ChatBot, it uses the ReQueue mechanism to transfer calls from Virtual Agent to Live Agent.  When the chat initially connects to Virtual Agent (TPPVA), the customer comes as an “unidentified” user. During the self-service offered by IW/ME in VIVR/Chatbot, the customer gets “identified” and “authenticated” with different mechanisms like “NRIC”, “CIF”, and “OTP”.  The data collected from customers (using “form” nodes in VIVR or from Module Engine calls to customer APIs) are saved into “session variables” in TPPVA.  During the self-service flow, the self-service may end by disconnecting the chat (by customer or agent), or by transferring to a live agent.  Saving Data To CHAT_CALL_HISTORY table  When the self-service ends in TPPVA (disconnect or transfer), the session data is saved into CHAT_CALL_HISTORY table.  TPPVA maps below data to each column in the table.  STARTDATETIME:  chat connect time to TPPVA ENDDATETIME:  chat disconnect to transfer time from TPPVA CALL_DUR:  Time between start and end (in seconds) CLID:  “phonenumber” – variable assigned from the Form Node  “node” – a json key/value (key=node) comes in input user json during chat start  When the channel is WhatsApp, then the WhatsApp mobile number  If chat ends with a transfer, then based on mapping configured in “UserDataMapping” or in “DataMapping” JSON file (UserDataMapping takes precedence over DataMapping JOSN) – parameter ‘mobile’  “mobile” variable updated from a custom DLL module called from IW flow (please refer to stackoverflow ….)  DNIS:  intent of the VIVR SessionID:  chat session id TR_DIS_FLAG:  disconnected reason (DC – disconnect, AT – transfer) LAST_MENU_ID:  lase IW menu LANGUAGE:  the selected language (if “language” variable was assigned in IW/ME). Default “English” CIF:  pCIF variable in user json data during chat start  “cif” variable assigned from a IW form node  If chat ends with a transfer, then based on mapping configured in “UserDataMapping” or in “DataMapping” JSON file (UserDataMapping takes precedence over DataMapping JOSN) – parameter ‘CIF’  Based on “DataMapping” json “IvrCallHistory” mapping – parameter ‘CIF’  “CIF” variable updated from a custom DLL module called from IW flow (please refer to stackoverflow ….)  EMP_NAME:  pUserId parameter in incoming chat json data  Based on “DataMapping” json “IvrCallHistory” mapping – parameter ‘EMP_NAME’  CUSTOMER_SEGMENT:  If chat ends with a transfer, then based on mapping configured in “UserDataMapping” or in “DataMapping” JSON file (UserDataMapping takes precedence over DataMapping JOSN) – parameter ‘CustomerSegment’  “CustomerSegment” variable updated from a custom DLL module called from IW flow (please refer to stackoverflow ….)  Based on “DataMapping” json “IvrCallHistory” mapping – parameter ‘CUSTOMER_SEGMENT’  NRIC:  “nric” variable assigned from a IW form node  If chat ends with a transfer, then based on mapping configured in “UserDataMapping” or in “DataMapping” JSON file (UserDataMapping takes precedence over DataMapping JOSN) – parameter ‘NRIC’  Based on “DataMapping” json “IvrCallHistory” mapping – parameter ‘NRIC’  LASTMENU_x:  the last IW menus executed TRANSFER_VDN:  if the chat ends with transfer, the Skill/VDN number COMPANY:  Based on “DataMapping” json “IvrCallHistory” mapping – parameter ‘COMPANY’ CUSTOMER_STATUS:  Based on “DataMapping” json “IvrCallHistory” mapping – parameter ‘CUSTOMER_STATUS’ TPIN_VERIFIED:  Based on “DataMapping” json “IvrCallHistory” mapping – parameter ‘TPIN_VERIFIED’ OTP_VERFIFIED:  Based on “DataMapping” json “IvrCallHistory” mapping – parameter ‘OTP_VERFIFIED’ PHONE_CODE:  Based on “DataMapping” json “IvrCallHistory” mapping – parameter ‘PHONE_CODE’ Example:  Let’s say we want to save a IW session variable called “myPhoneCode” to the PHONE_CODE column of CHAT_CALL_HISTORY table, then we have to add below configuration to TPPVA:  DataMapping.json -> IvrCallHistory  "PHONE_CODE": "SessionVar.myPhoneCode" Transfer Data to TMAC via ReQueue  After the customer is identified, if there is an “Agent Node” in IW flow, the chat gets transferred to Live Agent. This transfer between TPPVA (Virtual Agent) and TMAC (Live Agent) is done using a “ReQueue Request”.  TPPVA sends this “ReQueue” request to TComm Server (via TMAC Server) and TPPVA can send some data to TMAC server text chat interaction with ReQueue request.  The data that can be transferred from TPPVA to TMAC during the live agent transfer depends on the “SessionInfoHanlder” settings of TComm server. In this article, we discuss only the  “SelfServiceHandle” which is a generic handler used while VIVR/Chatbot in use.  Below are the properties supported by SelfServiceHandler:  nric, cc, cif, mobile, custSegment, customerName, pIntent, uuid, param1, param2, param3, param4, param5 When the TPPVA prepare the “ReQueue” request, TPPVA can fill these properties with data:  param2 – this parameter will have all the TPPVA session variables as a key/value collection  param3 – this will have the original user json data sent from VIVR/chatbot  param4 – this will have the “mobile” number property  param5 – this will have agent route parameters  customerName - based on mapping configured in “UserDataMapping” or in “DataMapping” JSON file (UserDataMapping takes precedence over DataMapping JOSN) – parameter ‘customerName’  mobile - based on mapping configured in “UserDataMapping” or in “DataMapping” JSON file (UserDataMapping takes precedence over DataMapping JOSN) – parameter ‘mobile’  When the chat gets assigned to TMAC Live Agent, the incoming chat user data contains above data passed from TPPVA.  From all these data available in the json, TMAC server has to pick some specific data to be saved in GBL_InteractionHistory:  These data are:  NRIC - nric  CIF - cif  CLID – regno1  TMAC server can assign data coming from the TPPVA to above three columns based on a config:  In TMAC server config there are two keys:  Chat_UseConfigToDeserializeChatData – this should be set to 1  Chat_JsonDataConfigFile – a file containing the mapping  In this mapping file, we can specify the mapping. See below example:  chatJsonConfig.config  salute=pNationality name=pName nric=pNric seg=pCustomerTag subseg=pCustomerTag cif=pCIF lang=pLang authtype=pAuthType callstatus=pName intent=pIntent regno1=pMobileNumber regno2=pMobileNumber vachatid=vachatid QUEUE_TIME=QUEUE_TIME custenttype=pIntent SubChannel=chatmode Channel=chatmode ChatMode=chatmode In this example, the “nric” is read from a json variable “pNric”.  However, when the chat is transferred from TPPVA to LiveAgent, we cannot send a parameter called “pNric” because the SelfServiceHandler does not support that parameter. So, we have to chose a parameter supported by the SelfServiceHandler. See below example:  Example:  For example, we can chose the parameter “customerName”.  Let’s say the nric is captured into a variable called “tempNric” in Iw/ME.  We can follow below configurations to use “customerName” to propagate the NRIC to TMAC.  In TPPVA: DataMapping.json-> CustomerData section "customerName": "tempNric”  If the TPPVA has “UserDataMapping.json”, then: "customerName": "tempNric"  In TMAC Server: chatJsonConfig.config nric=customerName Config files involved:  TPPVA:  UserDataMapping - UserDataMapping.json  DataMapping – DataMapping.json  TMAC:  chatJsonConfig.config

question: How can we configure custom actions for an incoming voice call in TMAC
answer: TMAC server has a feature that allows configuring a set of custom actions that can be executed when an incoming voice call comes.  To enable these actions, first set below app config to "1" in TMAC server tempalte.config:  <add key="Voice_PerformActionsForIncomingCalls" value="1" />  Then we can start configuring the actions.  Actions can be executed based on different parameter value combinations. We can configure any number of action sets (for different parameter combinations).  First set the number of different action sets we plan to have in below config:  <add key="Voice_IncomingCallActionsCount" value="2" />  In the above example, we specify that we will have two different action sets.  When configuring actions set, there are a few things we need to configure:  Action Rules:  Action rules are the combination of parameter values that decides if the action set should be executed.  Actions rules are added in config in below format:  <add key="Voice_IncomingCallActionRules_X" value="" /> -this "X" should be replaced with the actual rule number (1,2,3 etc)  Rules are written in the format of "SQL expressions".  There are few pre-defined parameters we can use here:  ANI - caller number - {0}  DNIS - called number - {1}  Call Type - type of the call (ACD or none ACD - 0/1) - {2}  UUI - UUI data of the call - {3}  For example, if we want to execute a set of actions based on below condition:  "If the ACD (calltpye=1) call coming from a number '40010' or '40011' and the UUI starts with 'CALLBACK' then perform the actions"  This example can be written like below:  <add key="Voice_IncomingCallActionRules_1" value="'{2}' = '1' AND '{0}' IN ('40010','40011') AND '{3}' LIKE 'CALLBACK%'" />  Actions:  Actions are the set of different actions which can be executed when a rule is matched.  Actions are configured in below format:  <add key="Voice_IncomingCallActions_X" value="" /> - this "X" should be replaced with the actual rule number (1,2,3 etc)  There are a set of pre-defined actions supported by TMAC:  answer - answer the incoming call  drop - drop the call  sleep - wait for configured time (sleep=10000 will wait for 10 seconds)  status - change the agent status (status=aux|10 will change agent statue to AUX 10)  none - do not perform any actions (used when we want to assign subchannel and subsessionid - see below - but do not want to execute any actions)  For example, if we want to:  "when a call comes in, answer the call, then change agent state to AUX 30, and wait for 5 seconds (5000 milliseconds) and drop the call" - we can write an action set for this like below:  <add key="Voice_IncomingCallActions_1" value="answer,status=aux|30,sleep=5000,drop" />  Sub Channel  When a rule is matched, then we can assign a "SubChannel" for that voice Interaction. This "SubChannel" get saved in TMAC_Interactions.SubChannel DB table coulmn.  <add key="Voice_IncomingCallActionSubChannel_1" value="Callback" />  Also this sub channel is sent to TMAC/AD UI in the IncomingCallEvent in the "SubType" property. The UI can also execute different logics based on this value.  Sub Session Id  When a rule is matched, then we can set the "SubSessionId" variable of the voice interaction from a property of Incoming Event.  <add key="Voice_IncomingCallActionSubSessionId_1" value="" />  This "SubSessionId" get saved in TMAC_Interactions.SubSessoinId DB table coulmn.  Also this sub session id is sent to TMAC/AD UI in the IncomingCallEvent in the "SubTypeData" property. The UI can also execute different logics based on this value.  Below are the set of available properties in Incoming Event:  MonitorHandle, PhoneNumber, UCID, UUI, CallType, CalledDevice, OrigPhoneNumber, OrigUCID, OrigCalledDevice, CallID, ConnectionHandle, Queue, Cause  Use case:  We can use these rules and actions to identify a callback or droprequest which gets assigned from the "Dialler" to TMAC. Dialer uses phantom phone numbers (ANI) to dial the calls. For example, let's says dialer uses ANI as 40010 and 40011.  When a dialer call comes to TMAC, it has to auto answer the call. And then the agent has to be put to some special AUX and the the call should be automatically dropped.  At the same time, some event data should be sent to TMAC UI to understand this is a dialer call. Also some data should be saved into DB tables to identify this call is a dialer call. <add key="Voice_PerformActionsForIncomingCalls" value="1" /> <add key="Voice_IncomingCallActionsCount" value="1" /> <add key="Voice_IncomingCallActionRules_1" value="'{2}' = '1' AND '{0}' IN ('40010','40011') AND '{3}' LIKE 'CALLBACK%'" /> <add key="Voice_IncomingCallActions_1" value="answer,status=aux|31,sleep=5000,drop" /> <add key="Voice_IncomingCallActionSubChannel_1" value="Callback" />

question: How does TMAC auto ACW feature works? How do we configure ACW for agents?
answer: How Does TMAC Auto ACW feature work? When TMACServer receives an incoming interaction "CreateIncomingInteraction" method will be called This method creates all the required events and send to TMACUI.  the Aux status of the Agent receiving this interaction will be "OnCall" And any AuxChange command pushed from tmac will be put to Pending Aux status for this specific agent.  using this feature of CM, TMACServer has implemented Auto ACW feature which pushes the ACW status from tmacserver in "CreateIncomingInteraction" method before the incomingcall events are formed and sent to TMACUI.  you might have a question here, What if the AutoAnswer is not enabled and Call dies on ringing state on tmacui ie. Agent hasnt picked up the call. according to the above mentioned logic Status will be changed from Available -> ACW without the Agent Answering the call.  To prevent the above scenario from happening there is a specific conditon in "CreateIncomingInteraction" method which check if AutoAnswer is enabled before sending the ACW AuxChange Command(pending Aux).  ie.  If AutoAnswer is enabled then ACW Aux change command (Pending Aux) is triggered at "CreateIncomingInteraction" method As the call is already answered and the agent should go to ACW post "OnCall" status  if AutoAnswer is disabled(Manual Answer) Then Auto answer command is not triggered at "CreateIncomingInteraction" method But is Triggered at OnConnected method which will be triggered when the Agent clicked the answer call btn and Call is being Answered.  Configuring the Auto ACW:  there are 4 scenarios which needs to be addressed for when answering this question  Auto ACW for all calls (IsVoiceAllAutoACWEnabled): if this is enabled Agent will go from OnCall to ACW after all the Call  Auto ACW for just ACD calls(IsVoiceACDAutoACWEnabled): If this configuration is enabled Agent will go from OnCall to ACW only after ACD Call  Auto ACW for Outbound calls(IsVoiceOutAutoACWEnabled): If this configuration is enabled Agent will go from OnCall to ACW only after Outbound Call  Auto ACW for TCamp calls(TCampPreviewCallAutoACWEnabled): If this configuration is enabled Agent will go from OnCall to ACW only after TCAMP Calls

question: How does the TMAC to IVR transfer for TPIN/OTP works?
answer: When an agent receives an incoming call from a customer or makes an outbound call to the customer using Agent Desktop or TMAC UI, sometimes agents are required to collect some secure data from the customer to authenticate the customer. Some of these data might be personal data that cannot be shared with an agent (such as telephone pin, NRIC ID).  In such a scenario, the agent can transfer the customer to an IVR flow that collects these secure data and authenticate the customer within the IVR without involving the agent.  TMAC (Agent Desktop and TMAC UI) provides an "IVR Transfer" feature for agents to transfer an incoming or outbound call to an IVR VDN. The most common two IVR transfers are TPIN transfer (IVR authenticates the user with a telephone pin) or OTP transfer (IVR authenticates the user with OTP sent to mobile).  In TMAC UI/Agent Desktop UI, there is a list of IVR transfer endpoints that can be configured using the Agent Desktop JSON. See below sample AD JSON:  "IVR": { "MenuEnabled": true, "DefaultMenu": [ "Main Menu", "Products", "Mobile", "Agent" ], "Transfer": { "Allowed": true, "Menu": [ { "Text": "Accesscode+TPIN", "Type": "v_nv", "Value": "tpin", "Icon": "lock" } ] } }, When the agent clicks the IVR transfer option in the IVR transfer menu, AD/TMACUI calls the TMAC server "TransferToIvr" method with the "value" in above Menu ("tpin" in this example).  When transferring a call to IVR, there are two different modes.  Agent Trasnfer the call to IVR and move to next call  Agent Trasnfer the call to IVR and waits for IVR to send the call back to agent (for TPIN/OTP authentication calls) - this is called "transfer with aux"  For TMAC server to identify the mode of transfer, there is a configuration in TMAC server template.conig called "Voice_IVRTransferTypesRequiresAux". This config contains a comma separated list of "values" which would be considered as mode #2 (transfer and wait for the call to come back to agent).  sample:  <add key="Voice_IVRTransferTypesRequiresAux" value="tpin,opt,vb" />  First TMAC identified the mode of transfer.  Then TMAC server tries to get a record from "AGT_IVR_Transfer_VDNs" table based on the provided "value". The DB record returns a "VDN".  For mode #1 above, TMAC does a blind transfer to IVR VDN. And the agent can close the tab and move to next call.  For mode #2 above, TMAC has to perform several actions.  First TMAC will get the VDN number from the above table.  Then TMAC server prepares the transfer UUI based on the uui.config. For IVR Transfers with AUX enabled, the UUI should contain the "AgentId", "InteractionID" and the "Original VDN" of the call. These values are injected to UUI based on the "uui.config" file inside TMAC server folder.  (Latest version of TMAC server >= 5.1.4.15 can inject the original UCID also to the transfer UUI).  Once the UUI is prepared, then TMAC server tries to find a AUX code matching to the transfer "value" (ex: tpin). These values are configured in DB table "AGT_AUX_Codes" (with value=tpin in this example).  If the aux code is found, then TMAC server first changes the agent state to that aux. If aux code was not found then AUX-0 will be used as default.  Since the agent is still on-call, the state will goto a "pending" state and wait for the call to get dropped from agent station.  After changing the the agent state to "pending-aux", then TMAC server performs a "Blind Transfer" to IVR VDN with the updated UUI.  If the blind transfer is successful, then TMAC server immedialty starts a wait timer which will wait for number of seconds configured in TMAC server template.config "TransferAUXTime" value. Usually this value should be greater than the time it might take for customer to complete the IVR flow and connect back to agent. If the this wait timer times out before the IVR send the call back to agent, then a event "AUXTimerEvent" is send to AD/TMAC UI.  Also, the agent will be pushed to the AUX state which was configured in "AGT_AUX_Codes".  Now the IVR starts promoting the user to enter the details for authentication. IVR may use the "Original VDN" number (and/or the Original UCID) entered in the UUI from TMAC serer before blind transfer to decide the IVR flow.  Meantime the agent waits for the call to come back from IVR.  Once the IVR completes the processing of the call, IVR has to send the call back to agent. To identify the agent, IVR uses the UUI's AgentID data section. And then IVR does a blind transfer back to "agent id" with updated UUI with new authentication status/data. The UUI may have the agentid and the interaction ID as well (in some IVR implementations, these data can be wiped out before the call is sent back to agent).  When the IVR transfers the call back to "agent id", the call will comes to agent's phone but it will start rining based on the "DAC - direct agent calling" settings configured in the Avaya CM. Based on this DAC settings, the call will be offered to agent's phone. Since the agent is on "AUX" state, and the IVR transfers the call to "agent id" (not the station id), the call is considered as a ACD call (based on DAC settings). If the agent is in on AUX when call comes to the phone, the phone will park the call and show an indicator to agent. Then the agent has to goto "Available" state to receive the call on AD/TMAC.  Or (based on DAC settings), the agent might get the call directly on AD/TMAC UI without getting parked on the phone.  Either way, when the TMAC server gets the new call, it first checks the UUI for agent id and the interaction ID based on "uui.config".  If the "interaction ID" is found in the UUI, then TMAC looks for the same interaction in agent session. If the Interaction is found (which means the agent has not closed the interaction yet), then TMAC does not create a new interaction. Instead it used the same interaction and send an "IncomingCallUpdateEvent" to the AD/TMAC UI (other events such as UUI data, IVR data also will be processed subsequently). In the AD/TMAC UI the existing interaction tab will be updated with new data.  If the Interaction ID is not found in UUI or the interaction ID is not found in agent session, then a new interaction is created and agent will get the call in a new UI interaction tab (AD/TMAC UI).

question: How does Work Queue ACK (Acknowledgement) work?
answer: Tetherfi Work Queue “ACK” feature ensures that a work item is delivered to the TMAC/Agent Desktop UI without fail. When a new item is added to queue, the item is removed from the queue only after the item is routed to the TMAC/AD UI and WQ receives and ACK from the UI.  EMM, TComm adds item to work queue.  In workqueue template.config there are two configs  <add key="AcknowledgementRequired" value="1"/>  <add key="WorkItemTTL" value="15000"/>  If “AcknowledgementRequired” is set to 1, then WQ will add items to queue with ACK enabled.  And the “WorkItemTTL” is the time in milliseconds WQ waits for an acknowledgment from the UI.  If this “WorkItemTTL” is not set or set to 0, then WQ will use the default value “20000” (20 seconds).  After WQ adds the items to queue with ACK enabled, and when the TMAC server receives this WQ item, TMAC server adds a ACK section to the interaction construct event (TextChatIncomingEvent, IncomingEmailEvent)  "ACK": { "IsRequired": true, "Source": "workqueue", "Id": "dev210930234153_2618", "Channel": "TextChat" }, When the TMAC JS SDK receives this interaction construct event, the SDK checks for this “ACK” property and if the “IsRequired” parameter is set to “true”, the SDK calls TMAC proxy method “EventAcknowledgement” method.TMAC SDK proxy forwards this method to TMAC Server.  When the TMAC JS SDK receives this interaction construct event, the SDK checks for this “ACK” property and if the “IsRequired” parameter is set to “true”, the SDK calls TMAC proxy method “EventAcknowledgement” method.TMAC SDK proxy forwards this method to TMAC Server.    public static CommandResultEvent EventAcknowledgement(string agentId, string channel, string itemId, string source)  agentId – id of the agent who received the event  channel – interaction channel  itemId – session id of the item  source – workqueue    If the source it “workqueue”, then TMAC will forward this method to WQ server.  The WQ will wait for the number of milliseconds configured in “WorkItemTTL”. If the ACK comes before the TTL the item is removed from the queue, else the item will remain in the queue and it will be routed to next agent.

question: IVR to TMAC Data Transfer
answer: Data Transfer Between IVR and TMAC After IVR finishes processing a call, it can route/transfer the call to an agent/ACD queue and then the call gets routed to TMAC. When this call transfer happens, the TMAC server and the UI should get the customer and interaction details processed by the IVR. There are several ways IVR sends data to TMAC:  Using TSAPI UUI Data Using Database Tables Using Redis Cache (TCacheManager) Using TSAPI UUI Data:  IVR can write some data to the UUI (User to User Information) which comes to the TMAC server along with Incoming Call Event. The UUI has a length limitation. Usually the max UUI size is 96 characters. So, the IVR and TMAC should come to an agreement and decide what data should be passed in the UUI. Usually, it comes as a single string with each data point in UUI occupying some exact predefined length. TMAC uses a configuration file called “uui.config” to parse the UUI string and then send the data to TMAC UI/Agent Desktop as part of “UUIDataEvent”. The TMAC UI/Agent Desktop displays these data based on the customer requirements.  UUIDataEvent: { "CallerName": "", "AuthType": { "AuthCode": "I", "IsIdentified": false, "IsVerified": false, "VerificationType": "Not Identified", "IsTPINVerified": false, "SiebelPIN": "N", "SiebelTPIN": "N" }, "CIF": "            ", "Language": "E", "NRIC": "                ", "Segment": "M   ", "OtherData": "                ", "EventName": "UUIDataEvent", "InteractionID": 1000, "IsInteractionConstructEvent": false, "IsInteractionDisposeEvent": false, "CreatedTime": "2021-09-30T17:34:54.8356539+08:00", "EventId": "6f69f5ef-6092-47b0-a639-550bf5b82147", "RecoveryEvent": false, "QueuedEvent": false, "ACK": null, "Catagory": null } However, for UUI data to come in Incoming Call Event, IVR should be able to perform a successful CTI Transfer (using AES JTAPI Transfer method). If the IVR CTI transfer fails, TMAC will not receive the UUI data along with the call.  Using Database tables IVR writes data into several tables and TMAC can read these data when a call comes to TMAC. When IVR writes the data into tables, it uses the call UCID (session ID) as the unique identifier. And when TMAC receives the Incoming Call event, the same UCID should be present in the Incoming TSAPI call event. If the UCID is not the same, TMAC will not know if this call comes from IVR and it wont be able to read any data from database tables. Below are some of the tables shared between IVR and TMAC (IVR writes and TMAC reads):  GBL_IntentMapping - When IVR decides the “intent” of the call, it inserts a record to this table with UCID and the Intent.When the call reaches TMAC, it tries to read a record based on the UCID present in incoming call event. If the record is found, TMAC uses that Intent and send it to UI in “CallerIntentEvent”.If there is no record found in this table for the UCID, then TMAC creates a new Intent record and keep the intent name as “Default”. It is possible to override this “Default” name with the Queue Name by enabling TMAC server’s config “UpdateIntentWithSkillName”.  CallerIntentEvent: { "IntentName": "ReportLoss_CCDC", "IntentStatus": "", "EventName": "CallerIntentEvent", "InteractionID": 1000, "IsInteractionConstructEvent": false, "IsInteractionDisposeEvent": false, "CreatedTime": "2021-09-30T17:34:54.8512727+08:00", "EventId": "e543d84e-52ab-4837-a995-ee9a7342e477", "RecoveryEvent": false, "QueuedEvent": false, "ACK": null, "Catagory": null } IVR_CALL_ACTIVE IVR writes call details to IVR_CALL_ACTIVE table before transferring the call to TMAC. The unique identifier for the record is UCID. TMAC uses the UCID received in the Incoming Call event to query the IVR_CALL_ACTIVE table and reads below data and sends IVRDataEvent to TMAC UI. DNIS, Last 4 Menus, UUI (if IVR has inserted the UUI), QueueTIme (a calculated queue time)  IVRDataEvent: { "LastMenu": "ReportLossMenu_CC_DC", "LastMenu_2": "MainMenu_ReportLoss", "LastMenu_3": "LanguageSelection_english", "LastMenu_4": "", "DNIS": "62222121", "QueueTime": "00:00:18", "UUI": "                                                  IEM                                           ", "CustomData": "", "EventName": "IVRDataEvent", "InteractionID": 1000, "IsInteractionConstructEvent": false, "IsInteractionDisposeEvent": false, "CreatedTime": "2021-09-30T17:34:54.8512727+08:00", "EventId": "6a5370e1-8a8e-45f3-bc8b-4e4c4e31931d", "RecoveryEvent": false, "QueuedEvent": false, "ACK": null, "Catagory": null } If there is no record found in the table for the UCID in an incoming call event, TMAC will not send any IVRDataEvent to the UI.  Using Redis Cache IVR can write data to Redis cache by calling the Tetherfi TCache Manager API. And these data is saved against the UCID. When TMAC server receives the call, it tries to read data from the Cache based on the UCID received in incoming call event. IVR saves the data to cache in below key. AGENTNODEDATA:<ucid> The data can contain anything related the IVR call. The data is then sent to the TMAC UI with “InteractionDataEvent” in the “AgentTransferData” property.

question: How does TMAC server or any other component licensing work?
answer: TMAC server has three different licensing modes:  Instance License  Evaluation License  Developer License  Instance License  An instance License is the preferred type of license for the TMAC server. The license is generated by the Tetherfi product team for a provided MAC address of a server. The request to generate the license has to be sent to the product team (there is a designated email address for this) along with required details (customer details, MAC address of the server).  The product team will create the license file and share it with the implementation team. The license comes in a form of a “.lic” file which has to be placed in the Tetherfi License Server folder.  After placing the license file into the Tetherfi License Server/Manager, the Licence server has to be restarted. The Licence server can successfully start only if the license is valid.  During the server startup, the TMAC server tries to connect to licensing server to acquire a valid license. If the license server is not present or if it is stopped (due to an invalid license), the TMAC server will not be able to acquire the license and the TMAC will fallback to next licensing mode (Evaluation License).    TMAC connects to the License server's WCF (HTTP) interface using "TetherfiLicClient.dll". The DLL should match the License Server version.  Below configuration is used in TMAC server to configure license server url:  <system.serviceModel> <client> <endpoint address="http://localhost/LicenseServer/" binding="basicHttpBinding" bindingConfiguration="basicHttp" contract="TetherfiLicenseServer.ITetherfiLicService" name="LicenseServer1" /> </client> </system.serviceModel> Evaluation License  The Evaluation license mode can be used for demo and POC purposes. It is not recommended to be used in SIT/UAT/Production systems.  The evaluation license can be generated for TMAC server by the product development team. To generate an eval license, you have to provide the MAC address, IP address, and the expiry date requirement to the product team. Based on the provided data, the product team can generate an evaluation license Key and share it.  The generated evaluation license key has to be placed in template.config file of the TMAC server.  <add key="EvalLicenseKey" value="place your key here" /> And the IP of the server (which was provided to product team) should be configured in below:  <add key="EvalLicenseLocalIP" value="10.1.1.10" /> This IP should be a valid IP assigned to any of the network interfaces of the server. If there is an IP change, then you must get a new eval license key.  The evaluation license takes the second precedence during TMAC server start-up. If the TMAC server was not able to acquire the license from the License Manager/Server, then it looks for an evaluation license in the above “EvalLicenseKey”. The key is then extracted to get the MAC ID, IP, and the expiry date of the key. And these data is then validated against the current server’s MAC ID, IP, and the system date time.  If all the validations are passed, then TMAC server will start successfully, else TMAC will fallback to the next licensing mode (Developer license).  Developer License  The developer license is generally used during the development and testing teams only. Using the development license mode, TMAC can be started without a License Server or an evaluation license. This gives the flexibility to the developers to run the TMAC server in any environment.  The developer license can be configured in the below key in TMAC server template.config.  <add key="Developer" value="Add the developer license key here" /> Number of agent sessions allowed: The license returned from License server has a property called "MaxAgentsAllowed" and TMAC will allow that many agent sessions to be created per TMAC server instance. If there is no license server used, then TMAC will use the config "AgentSession_MaxAgentsAllowed" to determine the max number of sessions allowed per TMAC server.

question: How can I use TMAC Server to host a custom DLL and call that from another application?
answer: TMAC Server has the provision to host a custom DLL which can be accessed via the TMAC proxy. Using this mechanism we can implement custom application logic just by creating a C# DLL without worrying about hosting it as an API. Below example shows a class with two methods:  Special Notes:  The method should return "string" value only. Complex objects return is not supported. To return a complex object, you can serialize it as a JSON string and return.  Make sure you wrap the whole method in with a try/catch block. Any unhandled exception in this dll can cause a TMAC server crash.  You can use Tetherfi Logger library to implement logging.  If you need any configurations to be read from app.config, make sure the key names have a unique prefix to differentiate it as a custom code. For example, key = "CustomInvokeTestApp_APIUrl"  See below example:  namespace CustomInvokeTestApp { public class MyClass { public string MyMethod1() { return "ok"; }  public string MyMethod2(string p1, string p2) { return "ok" + p1 + p2; } } } There are two methods, one with no parameters and the other with parameters. The return type for both are “string”.  This code is compiled as a DLL (DotnetFramework 4.0 to 4.6.2) and copied to TMAC Server application folder. (for example, above samle code compiled to a DLL called “CustomInvokeTest.DLL”  Any application can invoke the above methods by calling TMAC Http Proxy or TMAC SDK Proxy method as below:  TMAC Http Proxy:  Request:  • Url:'https://dice.tetherfi.cloud/tmachttpproxy/TmacProxy.asmx/InvokeCustomMethod'  • Method: POST  • Header: 'Content-Type: application/json'  • Body:There are 4 parameters required   target = “<dll name>:<namespace>:<class>”   method = “<method name>”   serializedParameters = “<parameters as an array>” – optional (required only when the method has parameters. Else keep empty   tmacServer = “<tmac server id>” – optional. Required only if you want to send the request to a scpefic TMAC server. If kept empty then the proxy will send the request to any available TMAC server.  Sample curl request below:  curl -X POST \'https://dice.tetherfi.cloud/tmachttpproxy/TmacProxy.asmx/InvokeCustomMethod' \--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \--data-raw '{"target":"CustomInvokeTest:CustomInvokeTest:MyClass","method":"MyMethod1","serializedParameters":"","tmacServer":""}'   Response:  The response will come in below format:  { "d": "ok" } The actual data is wrapped inside parameter “d”. Sample code to call a method with two parameters: curl -X POST \'https://dice.tetherfi.cloud/tmachttpproxy/TmacProxy.asmx/InvokeCustomMethod' \--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \--data-raw '{"target":"CustomInvokeTest:CustomInvokeTest:MyClass","method":"MyMethod2","serializedParameters":"['hi1','there']","tmacServer":""}' curl -X POST \'https://dice.tetherfi.cloud/tmachttpproxy/TmacProxy.asmx/InvokeCustomMethod' \--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \--data-raw '{"target":"CustomInvokeTest:CustomInvokeTest:MyClass","method":"MyMethod2","serializedParameters":"[\"hi1\",\"there\"]","tmacServer":""}'

question: How does TPPVA execute a module? What are the different ways of developing a module for a chat channel?
answer: In an IW chat flow, you can add a module. When TPPVA processes the chat flow, and when it receives the module node from IWE, then the TPPVA starts processing the module.  Different ways of module execution:  There are several ways of building a module.  Using Tetherfi Module Designer – MD is a UI similar to IW UI and you can create module flows using this UI. The modules created by MD are executed in Module Engine. – this is the preferred way of building a custom logic for a module  Using a flow file – a flow file is a structured file written in “.ini” format. Using a flow file you can create a simple chat flow including operations such as MENU, ANNOUNCEMENT, COMPARE, ASSIGN, QUEUE, DBWRITE, RESTAPI, etc. (please read the TPPVA design document for more details) – this method can be used for building quick and simple logics  Using a C# DLL – You can write your own code to execute a custom logic (module) using C# and compile it as a DLL. This DLL can be placed in TPPVA folder and invoked using the above flow file (please read the TPPVA design document for more details) – if the module engine is not an option due to various reasons (such as MD/ME not there in customer location), then you can chose this method  Using Java Self-Service Layer – this method was used a few years ago and is not recommended to use now. ME/MD should be used in place of the Java Self-Service Layer. When this method is used, a flow file has to be created and that will pass the execution to a Java API layer via a C# DLL called StandardModules.  When TPPVA receives a module node, first it checks if there is any “.flow” file in the same name as the module name in the TPPVA folder (ex: “Identification.flow”).  If there is a flow file, then the flow file is executed. If the flow file contains a DLL call, then the DLL is invoked.  If TPPVA does not find a flow file for the module name, then it will start executing the module in Module Engine.  However, the TPPVA config "ModuleEngineModules" can override above behavior. Even if there is a flowfile present, if the Module Name is present in "ModuleEngineModules" comma separated list, TPPVA will execute it using Module Engine.  Variables:  When TPPVA calls a module, all the variables collected in the session is passed to the module (to the DLL or the Module Engine) so that the custom logic can make use of those variables.  Also, the ME is used, it can assign new variables from the module and those variables get assigned to TPPVA session and can be used in IW or in other modules.  Module Exit:  After executing a module (using any of the above mechanisms), TPPVA has to exit the module and go back to IW to continue the flow. The exit happens based on the “exit nodes” configured for the module.  The module executor (flow file or ME) should define what is the exit node so that TPPVA can continue IW flow execution in that leg.  Example:  The below module validates an email address entered by the customer. The collected email address is saved in to a variable and passed to the module.  Few ways to implement the module:  Using a flow file: This module can be written using a flow file called ValidateEmail.flow and in the flow file you can add logic to compare the email address variable against some other hard coded values  Using dll: create a DLL extended from TPPVA CustomNodeBase class (refer to TPPVA design doc for more details), and write your validation logic. Create ValidateEmail.flow file and create a DLL node to call the validation method.  Using Module Engine: create a module in Module Designer and perform the validation by calling the DB connect API.  Once the operation is completed, it can set the exit node as one of the “Valid – valid email address”, “Invalid- invalid email address”, “Failed – operation failed” exit legs and TPPVA continues to IW based on that exit.

question: How does the Agent Desktop and Email manager handle email attachments?
answer: When Agent Desktop sends an email with an attachment below steps are executed:  Agent Desktop opens the email editor and clicks the upload button  User browse a file and select the file  Agent Desktop uploads the file to Tetherfi File Uploader (AD to File Uploader direct connection). In HA mode, the file upload URL will be an LB URL  In the file uploader, if s3 sync is enabled, the uploader will upload the file to s3  The file uploader generates a download link of the file and sends it back to the Agent desktop as a response  This download link generated by file uploader is a URL that points to Tetherfi Media Streamer (media steamer is another service that can download emails saved by the media uploader)  Agent Desktop adds this download URL taken from the upload response to the Email Send request body and call Send Email method.  The Send Email request comes to the Tmac SDK proxy and then the proxy forwards it to EMM  Once EMM receives the Send Email request, it starts processing the attachment URLs in the request  If the URL is an HTTP/HTTPS link, then EMM tries to download the file.  The download request goes to Tetherfi Media Streamer and if s3 was enabled then the media streamer gets the file from s3 and returns to EMM.  EMM gets the byte data of the file and injects it into the email send an object and calls SMTP or EWS send method with attachment to send the email

question: What is the purpose of Tmac Server signalr nat url?
answer: TMAC UI uses the SignalR NAT URL of the TMAC server to connect to the TMAC server's event socket (signalR WebSocket) when TMAC UI cannot directly connect to TMAC server's private IP.  TMAC UI connects to TMAC Server via a WebSocket to receive agent events from TMAC server to TMAC UI.  For this WebSocket implementation, the TMAC server uses the SignalR libraries( https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/signalr/overview/getting-started/introduction-to-signalr)  TMAC Server creates a SignalR listener endpoint and starts listening on that. There are two patterns used by TMAC Server when creating the singalR listener URL. Usually, the signalR endpoint name has the private IP of the TMAC server. Or it can have a wildcard (*) so that it listens on all the available IPs of the server.  template.config/TMC_Data.JSON  When Service Discovery Disabled:  key = "SignalrServerUrl"  value="https://<private IP of the server>/TMACSignalRServer" OR  value="https://*:443/TMACSignalRServer" (wild card)  When Service Discovery Enabled:  <add key="Listener_SignalrUrl" value="https://*:443/TMACSignalRServer" /> In both above examples, the listener URL will have a private IP of the server (for example 10.148.0.9). And the TMAC server sends this listener URL to TMAC UI as part for the login command response. And the TMAC UI now tries to connect to this signalR endpoint.  What if the TMAC UI cannot connect to the signalR URL? If the private IP of the TMAC server is not visible to the TMAC UI, then it cannot connect to signalR URL. In that case, TMAC UI has to connect to the TMAC server via some intermediate layer. This layer can be a proxy, a load balance, or a public IP assigned to the TMAC server.  TMAC server uses the "SignalRNATURL" configuration to keep this external visible SingnalR URL configured. And as part of login response, TMAC server sends this SignalRNATURL back to TMAC UI instead of the signalR listener URL.  template.config/TMC_Data.JSON  When Service Discovery Disabled: - both listener URL and NAT URL in same value and separated by a semi colon:  key = "SignalrServerUrl"  value="https://<private IP of the server>/TMACSignalRServer;https://<public IP of the server>/TMACSignalRServer" OR  value="https://*:443/TMACSignalRServer;https://<public IP of the server>/TMACSignalRServer"  When Service Discovery Enabled:  <add key="Listener_SignalrUrl" value="https://*:443/TmacServerSignalR" />  <add key="Listener_SignalrNatUrl" value="https://{NATIP}:443/TmacServerSignalR" />

question: What are the best practices for tagging?
answer: To help people looking for your question in the future (including your future self!), use existing tags if they apply. If appropriate, include a tag for product lines, specific projects, or internal teams that are relevant to the question.  The tags from the public Stack Overflow site are available for you convenience, so your Team can follow the same pattern of using technology-specific tags. question: Will public Stack Overflow users be able to see my Team?
answer: Teams on Stack Overflow are implemented on strictly segregated database schemas. Content on a Team can not be seen by anyone who is not signed up for your Team. That includes high-reputation users, moderators and even employees of Stack Overflow. Some employees have access to anonymous metadata about your Team, but that's limited under our terms of service and because we respect your privacy. It's our Prime Directive for Teams.  Nobody outside your Team can see that you are a member. Earning 200 reputation on the Team will grant you an association bonus if you haven't already earned it on another site on the network. But there's no indication of where you earned it.  We're always on guard against unauthorized access to private data. One step we take is to hire outside security experts who test our systems and look for vulnerabilities.

question: What is Stack Overflow for Teams?
